[question] D6-15: The critic's monthly calibration is a session nobody pressed Start for (on by default, a 'schedule' session on no project that spends on the model within its own cap); it does no project work, but the rule 'only the person starts a session' must name it; Owner's words: "the user clearly states when a session will run"; Where: jobs/calibration.ts:60-67, :285-300; ADR 0060; settings-view.ts:177-179.
decisions: S-1 Who asked is on every start: StartRequest.by = 'person' | 'schedule' | 'hands_off' | 'continuation' (append-only; 'continuation' is the person's own session going on after a credential wait, S-10; continues?: the session id a person start continues; trigger stays for the record), written on the session.started event and in the session row's plan JSON (plan.startedBy, append-only, no migration), which d1109-sessions words. Person starts: POST /sessions, session.start (chat, voice and phone), Approve and start (intake), Approve and start on the level 0/1 session plan card, Continue on a budget card, Use API key on a credential card (personStart / personContinue, called by d1109-cred-engine), Continue where it stopped, a session's Continue, the recovery Update's Continue, and a person start kept for a credential's reset. The daemon's Scheduler gets isQuietHours from a cached reader (QuietHours in compose.ts: notify_prefs.quiet_hours and the time zone, refreshed in the scheduler's refresh hook before every tick and when the settings route changes them; the port reads it synchronously); deferredNow holds every start that is not by 'person' (a continuation is held too: the person's Quiet hours setting promises 'no sessions that start on their own between these times', and a continuation starts with nobody pressing anything; it goes on once they end, S-10); enqueue keeps every person start and continuation; a schedule's fired key is written when its start leaves the waiting line (started, or queued behind a session), never while quiet hours hold it. The critic's calibration is named in the ADR as the one exception (by 'schedule', as today; the owner's answer 6 of 2026-11-09: it stays monthly and on, and the run indicator shows it with words saying what it does, d1109-run-visible V-1). Why: the owner's control needs one fact the scheduler can enforce; the Quiet hours setting promises 'no sessions that start on their own'; a job held in the night must still run once.

S-2 One function prepares work: prepareWork(deps, {agentId, projectId, taskIds, reason, by: 'person' | 'system' | 'agent'}) in a new session/prepared-work.ts replaces resumeWork's start in every answer path (person-questions, cannot-run, findings, pr-answers rebase and Redo, late approvals) and returns {outcome, line}; recordStart stores the outcome on the card for its Done line. Outcomes: joined, no_room, stopping, waits_start, stopped_all, started, queued, deferred, nothing_to_run, failed. Why: one place decides and one map of words says it (design §5 rule 10), so no answer path starts a session by its own logic again.

S-3 Budget raises and resets prepare: wakeBudgetWaits withdraws the card and makes the task ready, then calls prepareWork (by 'system') instead of resumeWork; a raise through Settings (monthly cap, project budget, the subscription's allowance) runs the wake at once and its change line says how many paused tasks are ready again and that they run at the next Start; once d1109-cred-engine (C5) makes the share a credential stop, a raised allowance ends that stop and its change line is d1109-cred-engine's (CE-6: it says when the person's waiting session goes on). Continue on a budget card stays a person start (personStart with the card's budget). Why: the owner: 'the user clearly states when a session will run'; a month reset can come weeks later, in the middle of the person's instructions.

S-4 CI results and PR comments start nothing, with the setting on or off: GitHostWatcher.fire no longer asks the scheduler; the events are delivered to the agent's inbox as today (deliver), the audit row records outcome 'waits_start', and the next session's brief reads them. Why: no start nobody asked for, and text a third party wrote never starts paid work; the information still reaches the next session (ADR 0075's content rule unchanged); the owner confirmed on 2026-11-09 (answer 9: 'fine') that they start none, also with 'Start a session by itself' on.

S-5 The hands-off setting: project.settings.start_by_itself, false by default for every project (no migration: absent is off); settings-view row 'When work is ready' with 'Wait for my Start' / 'Start a session by itself'; SETTING_SPECS entry (scope project, risk medium, narrows when off; turning on asks the yes with its effect line 'Sessions of Quote page will start by themselves when work you made ready can run, up to CHF 5.00 each. Never in your quiet hours or while sessions are stopped.'); settings.set refuses it for an agent actor. prepareWork and the budget and credential wakes read it; a start it makes is by 'hands_off', only for preparation by 'person' or 'system' (never by 'agent': D7's own tasks), with the project's session cap, after startBlocked (Stop all, no Claude, nothing runnable). A hands-off start held by quiet hours or queued behind another start is kept on the project (summary_cache.start_pending {since, why}, version-checked), asked again by a sweep in the scheduler's refresh hook once nothing holds it (after a restart too), and cleared when it starts. Why: the owner confirmed 'Only when you say so' as the default with the hands-off setting optional; per project so one project can run hands-off while another is shaped; a line that says 'It runs after your quiet hours.' must stay true across a Quit.

S-6 The promise is the Start dialog's list: promiseOf(check) in start-check.ts = runnable (cut as today, with d1109-oversize-pause's OP-0: the larger task at its place with its planned room, the tasks after it as after_large, and a task paused at a session's budget that this start takes in its turn) then later cut to the work budget left after runnable, in run order (the followers beyond it are named 'and N more wait for a later Start'); the runner computes the promise with the same function at its start (or takes the approved plan's tasks and followers, or, for a session's Continue, the remaining promise of the session it continues), emits session.promised {taskIds, estimateUsdMicro, afterLarge?} (afterLarge append-only: the after_large task ids) and keeps it on the plan row. The dialog's sentence reads the cut list and adds one line 'Work you make ready while it runs joins it if its budget has room.'; while another project's session runs, 'Starts after the session on "Quote page"'. Why: 'the session keeps its promise' needs the promise to be what the person saw when they pressed Start.

S-7 Join only if it fits: a live-session registry (new session/live-sessions.ts) where the runner registers an admit handle for its project. admit(taskIds, by) reads each task fresh: the session's own (promised and runnable by itself, or waiting for its Claude credential inside the session) -> joined; stopping, wrapping up, in its end review or closing -> stopping (the line 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.'; the task is added to notAgain so it does not run in that session); an oversized task (estimate above the whole work budget, D4) -> no_room (it cannot fit; it runs in its turn at the next Start, d1109-oversize-pause's OP-0); else room = work budget less spent less the remaining estimates of its own tasks and of what joined; estimate (priced as the planner prices) <= room -> joined (kept in the session's joined map, session.joined event), else no_room. closing: when the queue is empty the runner sets the handle's closing flag before its last replan and clears it only if that replan found work, so an admit between an empty replan and the session's end never answers joined. readmit(taskIds) takes credential-waiting tasks back as the session's own and clears notAgain for them (d1109-cred-engine's Use API key). A task the person pauses or cancels, or that needs the person's answer, gives its room back; bringing it back is a newcomer. D7's changes: the parts of a split promised task are the session's own up to the task's remaining estimate (a part beyond it is a newcomer); a step added before a promised task is a newcomer, and if it does not fit the promised task leaves the promise and both are named once in the result; a dropped duplicate frees its room; the task check's cost is admitted like a newcomer (room after the promise and what joined). replan takes its own tasks first (the tasks the start left 'after_large' behind a task larger than the work budget, d1109-oversize-pause's OP-0, are its own after that task: they hold no room while it runs, and once it has ended, done, failed or paused, each is taken in the plan's order by the room left), then joined, then newcomers re-admitted in priority order after each task ends; nothing else (today's 'every ready task that fits'). At levels 0 and 1 a person's preparation is added to onlyThese when it joins; anything the agent adds is not. The result's 'Left for your next Start: ...' and two log lines (event-lines.ts) say it. Why: option C keeps the promise and uses spare budget; deciding at the action makes the line true; admitting never raises a budget.

S-8 Edits apply before a task starts and never during its run: at the claim the runner refreshes the queue item from the claimed row (specialist, title, estimate re-priced) before chooseSpecialist and the start line; task.update of a running task keeps refusing its field changes but queues the note it carries and answers '"X" is running now: it is not changed mid-run; your note goes into its next attempt.' (today the refusal drops the note). Why: 'queue up tasks and then change things': a change made before the run must be the run; a change mid-run would mix two briefs.

S-9 Every preparing action says what happens next: the commands that make a task ready (task.transition to ready, task.resume, task.reopen, task.create with status ready, which Make this a task uses) call ports.prepareWork after their transaction and append its line to the sentence (the Tasks row shows change.sentence already, chat replies with it); chat's read-back of such a move adds a preview of the line (ports.previewWork, read-only). The Inbox's card explains are read when the card is shown: RequestWordsContext gains running ('this_project' | 'other' | null) and startsByItself, so Try again reads '...; it joins the running session if it fits.' or '...; it runs at your next Start.'. Make ready's and Resume's static explains become 'Ready to run: the running session takes it if it fits, else your next Start.' and 'It is ready again: the running session takes it if it fits, else your next Start.'. Why: design §5 rule 4 (true now) and rule 9 (no promise the code does not keep); the owner wants to know when a session will run.

S-10 A session the person started goes on by itself after a credential wait inside it (the owner's decision of 2026-11-09: 'that is what wait means'). When a Claude credential stops a task, the rest of the session's queue runs (only that task waits, runner.ts:1910-1925); when nothing else can run the session ends to wait as today; the executor's noteWait passes the session id, so the wait entry stores {projectId, agentId, since, sessionId}, and for a session by 'person' or 'continuation', or by 'schedule' of a schedule the person set (today the monthly handover test of a project the person turned it on for; the critic's calibration, on by default, is not one: its held call skips and stays due, d1109-cred-engine CE-10), the runner keeps its continuation on the entry ({by: 'continuation', continues: sessionId, budgetUsdMicro: its cap less the ledger's booked spend, the remaining promise}, version-checked; keepContinuation), unless the person stopped that session (Stop after this task or Stop now, from the app, chat, voice, the phone or the tray) or it was stopping or wrapping up when it ended to wait: such a session keeps no continuation and its waiting tasks read 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.'. At the stop's end (the reset, a raised allowance, the month's start for the share, a new key saved after a refusal: whatever ends the stop, d1109-cred-engine's settleStops once it merges) credentialWaits.wake makes that continuation exactly once, after a restart too and never twice: a start by 'continuation', held by quiet hours like every start the person did not press (it goes on once they end; every sentence that says when it goes on names the later of the stop's end and the end of the quiet hours, in the person's time zone: 'waiting until 07:00 (after your quiet hours), then it goes on'), with the rest of the promise and of the budget (never more; none when nothing is left or nothing of it can run), on the credential the policy allows (never another one unless the policy says go on with the next or a grant of that stop covers it: D5, d1109-cred-engine), admitting prepared work by S-7's rule; its first log line 'Goes on with your session of 14:05.'. Cancel (POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel), Stop all and the project's removal (w15-tail's guard, run B) drop it, and Make one project is refused while it waits (d1109-onerepo-join, C4, reads it). One wait per project: while a continuation or a kept start of the project waits, a person start of that project (POST /sessions, a session's Continue, chat's 'run it now', the phone) keeps nothing new and starts nothing and answers when it goes on ('Your session of 14:05 goes on by itself at 15:40.', or 'A session of Quote page starts at 15:40.' for a kept start; chat replies that line with no read-back); when the stop has ended and the wake has not run yet, the wake runs first; 'Use API key' (d1109-cred-engine, d1109-cred-screens) makes the waiting continuation go on now through personContinue; to start in another way the person presses Cancel first; after Cancel its tasks read 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.' and the ended session's Continue (its page, the project status line, Home) opens the Start dialog with continues = that session: the remaining promise and budgetUsdMicro = its cap less the ledger's booked spend (no Continue when that is zero or less). A wait entry without a person's session (work prepared outside a session the person started, the critic's calibration, a hands-off session's wait, an entry made before this change) prepares at the stop's end (prepareWork by 'system'), so a NEW session starts only by the person or by the hands-off setting (by 'hands_off', S-5). A person's Start, or a session's Continue, pressed while the credential is out and no continuation is kept ('Start at 15:40') keeps one person start on the entry ({by 'person', continues?, budgetUsdMicro}, keepStartAtReset), made once at the stop's end the same way (by 'person', so quiet hours do not hold it: the person chose that time). personContinue(sessionId), readmit(taskIds), keepStartAtReset and the kept continuation are the ports d1109-cred-engine (sub-run C5) calls (Use API key goes on now; Wait leaves the continuation kept). Row and card words: '...; then your session goes on.' while a continuation or a kept start waits, '...; then it runs at your next Start.' otherwise; d1109-run-visible (C5) shows the waiting continuation on the run indicator with Cancel. What a wait is, which credential serves next and whether the person is asked first stay D5's. Why: the owner decided that a session the person started keeps going by itself until its work is done, including after a credential wait inside it, shown while it waits with Cancel and never moved onto another credential unless the policy says so, while a NEW session after a stop the person did not start still needs the person or the hands-off setting; carrying the rest of the promise and budget keeps what the person gave the session they started.

S-11 Chat says start in words, and every start said in chat or voice is read back: session.start gets askFromChat (a yes from chat and voice at any budget, whether the parser or the chat model asked; the app's, the palette's and the phone's starts are no chat); the parser also maps 'run it now', 'run them now', 'run it', 'go ahead and run it', 'let's run it', 'start it' (and the German 'starte es', 'jetzt ausführen') to session.start; negations ('don't run it yet', 'I'll run it later', 'not yet') and task text ('add a task: run the tests') do not. The chat model's tool definitions change: session.start ('Start a work session now on the person's say-so; it is read back for their yes; answers and task changes never start one'), task.reopen, task.resume and task.transition ('it is ready again: it joins the running session if it fits, else it waits for the person's next Start'), settings_set's new key line. Why: the owner named 'run it now'; 'ok' or 'sounds good' read by a model is not the person stating when a session runs; tool definitions are model-facing code and must say what the app does.

S-12 Words: one map in prepared-work.ts (preparedLine, preparedExplain) used by request-words.ts (startWords and the cards' explains and Done lines), task-words.ts (budget-paused and credential-wait rows), result.ts (paused and credential lines, the left-for-next-Start line), credential-wait.ts (after-the-wait sentences) and the commands' sentences; no person-facing sentence says 'by itself', 'starts a session' or 'goes on' unless the setting, a kept start, the person's waiting session (the continuation) or the person's own Continue makes it true. Why: design §5 rules 4, 9, 10; the owner: 'a sentence promises only what the app does'.

S-13 ADR 0118 'Who starts a session' (D6, with D8's run indicator appended by d1109-run-visible in C5) records the rule and the owner's continuation, names the critic's calibration as the one exception on this computer (shown on the run indicator while it runs, d1109-run-visible, C5) and the cloud runner as a known gap (services/cloud-runner/src/inbox-trigger.ts still asks for a session with trigger 'message' on a new message or an answered request; it is brought in line in a later round), and amends 0053 (Approve and start on a session plan is a person start), 0060 (the calibration named as the exception; schedules held by quiet hours still run once), 0075 (CI and PR comments start no session; they reach the next session), 0088 (a late approval prepares; the next session consumes it), 0100 (a wait's end continues the person's own session that waited, with the rest of its promise and budget, and prepares everything else; a session's Continue carries its remaining promise and budget; a person start kept for the reset), 0102 point 2 (Tasks-row actions prepare), 0112 (a raised or reset limit prepares; Continue is a person start), each amendment dated. Why: AGENTS.md: decisions go in ADRs; the session lead edits design core-experience.md from design_doc_changes.
u_entries: New U-entry U-093 (the session lead writes it): 'Sessions start when I did not press Start' (answers, raises, a credential back, PR comments), with this area's Check in the app steps, including a session you started that waited for its Claude credential going on by itself at the reset (shown on the run indicator with Cancel after C5) and Cancel leaving it for your Start.
root_causes: packages/runtime/src/session/resume-work.ts: one helper starts (or queues) a session for every answer that makes a task runnable; every answer path calls it, so preparing work and starting work are the same act.

packages/runtime/src/session/triggers.ts and daemon/compose.ts: a start request carries only its trigger kind, not who asked, and the daemon's Scheduler is built without quiet hours, so a person's start and an automatic one are treated alike and the Quiet hours promise is not kept.

packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts: the session has no promise (replan takes whatever ready task fits the room left), no way for an action outside the runner to ask whether a task may join, and it runs the plan's snapshot of a task's specialist and estimate.
packages/runtime/src/wiring/billing-pick.ts and daemon/compose.ts: a credential wait is kept per project without the session it belongs to, so its end can only start a fresh, full-budget session.
packages/runtime/src/session/githost-watcher.ts and session/budget-card.ts: automatic producers call the scheduler directly.
The words: request-words.ts, task-words.ts, result.ts, credential-wait.ts and the commands each wrote their own 'starts a session' / 'goes on by itself' sentence for one behaviour.
packages/commands/src/commands/session.ts: session.start is read back only above a money line, so a start said in chat, or asked by the chat model, acts at once below it.
packages/runtime/src/session/triggers.ts: a schedule's fired key is written before its start and a quiet-hours hold lives in memory, so a hold that outlives the process loses the start.
areas.fix_scope: Run C sub-run C3 (wave 19; /tmp/frbench/runC-plan.json): base the merge of sub-run C2; built beside d1109-chat-depth from the same head (they meet only at C3's merge step, which merges in key order: this area is number 1); the shared_files rules naming C3 and '(run C)' decide every file two areas touch. Base: run C after sub-runs C1 and C2 (on wave 15 run B's merged head after 3600089): d1109-oversize-start and d1109-oversize-pause are merged, and d1109-oversize-pause's final spec writes no sentence that a raised or reset limit makes a task go on by itself (its outer-limit lines are this area's to reword); re-find every line named here (run B rewords many of the sentences this area changes, W15-65, W15-66 and W15-78 in credential-wait.ts and W15-38 in the Start dialog: start from its texts). Order: S-1, S-2, S-3, S-4, S-5, S-6, S-7, S-8, S-9, S-10, S-11, S-12, S-13. One commit per item: the failing test first at the person's boundary named in its acceptance line, then the fix, then the siblings (validation rule 8; log what you find). Boundaries: S-1 triggers unit cases (by on every request; deferredNow; the fired key written only when the start leaves the line) plus real-daemon cases (POST /sessions with quiet hours on starts; a hands_off start is held) and a restart case (a monthly job due inside quiet hours, the runtime composed twice inside them: it runs exactly once after them); S-2 real-daemon cases in a describe block 'd1109-starts-engine, run C' appended to apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, every card answered with requestView(row).options (never 'yes'), asserting GET /sessions and the scheduler log unchanged after two ticks and the Done line from GET /requests, one case per card kind (siblings), and a restart case (compose twice after the answer: the boot syncs start nothing); S-3 a real-daemon case with the simulated clock (raise the cap through the settings route; a new month) and the unit test of each budget sentence; S-4 a composed GitHostWatcher case on the fake host with the setting off and on; S-5 real-daemon (the settings route with the yes, an answer then starts one session; off, none; a task only D7 added, none; Stop all and quiet hours) plus restart cases (the setting; a held start composed twice inside quiet hours starts once after them); S-6 the start-check unit and a composed case comparing GET start-check with the session.promised event; S-7 a new composed test packages/runtime/test/session-join.test.ts (stand-in provider, fixed estimates: the promise kept, a joining Redo, a no-room task, spare budget re-check, a cancelled promised task, an oversized newcomer, the after_large tasks behind a larger task that fails at once, Stop after this task, level 1, the admit-versus-end race with an admit between the last empty replan and the session's end, a readmitted credential-waiting task, a split promised task and a step added before a promised task) and a real-daemon case for the Tasks-row line while a session runs, asserting the ledger never passes the cap or the review fifth; S-8 a composed case (Edit a queued task's specialist and criteria; the run row's specialist and the brief from the request builder) and the commands unit for the refusal that keeps the note; S-9 the commands unit for each command's sentence and real-daemon cases for POST /tasks/:id/action (make_ready, try_again, resume, go_ahead, redo, reopen) and POST /projects/:id/tasks in three states (a session of the project running with room, without room, none), and GET /inbox's explains with and without a running session; S-10 composed cases in the credential-wait tests with the stand-in subscription and the simulated clock (a person's session that ended to wait goes on by itself once at the reset, by 'continuation', with its budget left and the remaining promise, on the subscription, with no request to the key under wait; inside quiet hours it waits until they end; Cancel, Stop all and a removed project drop it; a Start while it waits keeps and starts nothing; a session the person stopped keeps none; a handover test session keeps one; after Cancel the session's Continue with its budget from the ledger; a wait entry of work outside a person's session prepares and starts nothing; a start kept by Start before the reset; the setting on; a legacy entry) and a compose-twice restart case before the reset (one continuation, made once; none after Cancel), plus real-daemon cases for POST /sessions with continues and POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel; S-11 the intent unit, a composed chat case at a CHF 1.00 budget and one where the stand-in chat model calls session_start after 'ok' and after 'sounds good' (nothing starts before Yes; Yes starts one), and the conversation request-builder test asserting the exact tool definitions the model receives; S-12 the unit test of each function that writes a sentence (exact strings, at most 100 characters, CHF, no id) plus a grep test over the words modules for 'by itself', 'starts a session' and 'goes on' outside the true cases; S-13 docs. Every changed or new route gets its real-daemon case and apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts changes in the same commit. Existing tests that assert today's behaviour (answers start sessions: resume-work, plan-approval, budget-pause, credential-limits, credential-wait-session, task-usage-limit, session-keeps-going, sandbox-waiting, subscription-path, signoff-answer, where-last-run-stopped, writing-rules, w15-chat-words, the githost-watcher cases, the UI's inbox, tasks, project and polish-screens tests, real-daemon cases) change with the design, each named in its commit; none is weakened or skipped. Money: admit never raises a budget and never uses the review fifth; a session's Continue (or a kept start) uses the cap less the ledger's booked spend, never more; a hands-off start uses the project's session cap and every outer cap (month, plan share) holds; when a line says it waits, nothing moves (assert no start and no spend). decisions: Three rungs above the quick answer's, one new mode in code, the model chosen by the need. Quick: today's fast pass unchanged (model, effort, thinking off at low, 1,024 tokens, ADR 0091's budget, d1109-chat-recall's 6 calls). Longer: the fast model one effort step up with adaptive thinking (medium, 4,096 output tokens a call, at most 8 model calls, 120 s): the same model, no switch. Stronger: a new mode chat_thorough in MODE_DEFAULTS (tier sonnet, effort medium with adaptive thinking, 4,096 output tokens a call, 120 s, at most 8 model calls, target total 30 s), added to MODE_VALUES, AGENT_SETTING_MODES, MODE_LABELS ('Chat, thorough answers') and the model settings view (ADR 0072: the person can move it to Opus or high effort); its effort held at the conversation agent's registry max_effort (medium, unchanged); its tier held at the project's highest model (outside a project the default ceiling, as chat today); when that leaves it at or below the fast pass's tier, the stronger rung is the longer one. Best: the project's highest model at chat_thorough's effort, when the person's words ask for the best or name that model, or offered through the ask line under a stronger answer that reached its wrap-up on a project whose highest model is above the stronger rung's (the need proposes it; the person's yes runs it). A deliberate limit: the need alone never starts on the best rung (no classifier tells a question that needs Opus from one that Sonnet answers well); every rung above the fast model's asks first anyway, so the escalation is one more ask line, never a silent switch. The need picks the rung, in code (rungOf), from answer_thoroughly's why or the person's words: many_records and the person's plain ask ('think it through' and the like) -> longer; failure, plan, comparison and review -> stronger; words naming a stronger model ('use a stronger model', 'use Sonnet') -> stronger; 'use the best model', 'use Opus' -> best. Why: the owner's answer 2 of 2026-11-09 ('Which model? whatever is appropriate'): the model follows the need, never above the project's highest; thinking longer on the same model is no switch, so it needs no yes (the ask rule).

Who decides. The person: words at the start or end of the line, outside quotes ('think it through', 'think harder', 'take your time', 'be thorough', 'look into it properly', 'in depth', 'use a stronger model', 'denk gründlich nach', 'nimm dir Zeit'), a bare phrase re-asking the person's previous line in this conversation ('Think through what? Ask your question first.' when there is none), and the Think it through button, which sends 'Think it through.' with depth 'longer' (its consequence line names about how long and the 'at most' the press allows: 'Thinks longer on this model: about 20 seconds, at most CHF 0.04.', on a Claude plan 'Thinks longer on this model: about 20 seconds on your Claude plan, at most CHF 0.04 at API prices.'; the press is the person's yes for that 'at most', which is the pass's budget); the plain words run the longer rung and words naming a stronger or the best model run that rung after the ask; 'quick', 'quickly', 'briefly', 'in one line', 'kurz' keep a line on the fast pass; a line the parser understands is a command as today. The fast model: one tool, answer_thoroughly {why: many_records | failure | plan | comparison | review | asked} (an enum: nothing the model writes is stored or shown), called before any lookup. Code always decides: it picks the rung from the need (the rungs decision), the model, the effort and the money, and whether to ask first (the ask rule). No keyword routing beyond the person's phrases and no classifier call. Why: the decision rides on the call that happens anyway; the person always has the last word; the person's phrases are a promise the code keeps the same way every time.

The gate for the fast model's ask, in order, each refused with 'Not now: <reason>. Answer as well as you can from what you have; the app offers a closer look under your answer.': a typed turn (voice and phone never; a spoken 'think harder' gets 'I can think that through in the chat: type it there.'); the person did not ask for a quick answer; the turn has no recordsRead (d1109-chat-guard's flag: no read or recall result yet, no card listed in full whose words Forerunner did not write, nothing flagged in the facts); the outer room (the caps port's room over the month cap, the plan share and the project's caps, as hooks.callRoomUsdMicro reads it) leaves a useful budget; a stronger rung or effort exists. The person's own ask skips the record check, never the room checks; what passes the gate then follows the ask rule, which also covers a credential that is not the person's first. Why: a record never starts a spend by itself (a card's quoted words are not scanned in the facts, agent.ts:1524 wraps only doc excerpts, so the flag, not the scanner, decides); until D5's policy is built, chat goes on with the next credential (ADR 0100 point 4), and an automatic answer must not spend on the API key while the person's first choice rests; money and safety are code; the reasons become the person's sentences.

The ask rule (the owner's answer 2 of 2026-11-09): before a stronger or the best rung (any switch of model), or a rung whose estimate is above the person's ask-above amount (chat_ask_above, default CHF 0.10; 'expensive' in the session lead's reading of the owner's words), chat asks first in one line with the cost and the time and goes on only on yes. On an automatic hand-over the turn ends with the fast pass's brief answer from what it has and, under it, the line; when the person's own line asked, the reply is the line alone. The line: 'This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.15 (at most CHF 0.30) and 20 seconds. Go ahead?' (a longer pass above the amount: 'This needs a closer look: about CHF 0.14 (at most CHF 0.28) and 40 seconds. Go ahead?') with Go ahead; Go ahead, or 'yes' or 'go ahead' typed as the next line in that conversation, runs that rung once on the same question (no second fast call); any other next line drops the offer with nothing spent; a Go ahead after a restart or after the room or the price changed re-reads both and asks again with the new figures when they changed. A longer pass within the amount goes ahead without asking, its waiting line naming the time and the cost, with Stop. Until d1109-cred-engine merges, a pass that would go ahead runs only on the person's first credential; on another one it asks, and the line names it ('This needs a closer look on your API key while your Claude subscription rests: about CHF 0.03 (at most CHF 0.06) and 20 seconds. Go ahead?'). On a Claude subscription the amount, the estimates and the pass budgets are the API-equivalent figures the ledger books for a subscription answer (the same prices; Forerunner's share and the session budgets count them so too), so 'expensive' means the same on both credentials and also covers using up the plan's limits; the line then names the plan and the API price: 'This needs a stronger model: about 20 seconds on your Claude plan (about CHF 0.15 at API prices). Go ahead?' ('This needs a closer look: about 40 seconds on your Claude plan (about CHF 0.14 at API prices). Go ahead?'), and the hand-over step 'Thinking it through with Sonnet on your Claude plan: about 20 seconds.'. Why: the owner's words 'as much as needed, but if it will switch models and do an expensive task, it should warn/ask first'; the yes is the person's, never the model's or a record's; one line with the cost and the time.

Money. No daily amount of chat's own and no fixed per-answer cap: the budgets and the monthly cap bound chat as every call (the owner's answer 2: 'as much as needed'). On a Claude subscription every amount below is the API-equivalent figure the ledger books for the answer (the ask rule). A pass's SessionBudget: for a longer pass that goes ahead without asking, min(the ask-above amount at the day's rate, the outer room), so no answer spends more than that amount without a yes; for a pass the person said yes to, min(the 'at most' its line named (twice the estimate, rounded up to the centime), the outer room); a budget below three worst cases of the pass's first call (the loop's own estimate: input as sent plus the whole 4,096 cap) is refused before any call, with the cap line. The estimate is the median cost of the last 20 answers on that rung and model in this install, rounded up to the centime, else the loop's estimate of five calls at the rung's prices on this context. The run hears the wrap-up once through the loop's wrapUp option (ADR 0112's mechanism, today absent for chat): 'Wrap up now: make no more lookups. Answer from what you have, and say in one sentence what you could not check.' so it always ends with an answer. Every call goes through the hooks (outer caps per call), the routed provider with purpose chat (the person's credential order; D5's policy when built) and the ledger, on the conversation session with the turn's project and run id '<turn id>:thorough'. Why: no budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or plan-share cap is passed; what a yes covers is its line's 'at most'; what goes ahead without a yes is at most the person's amount.

The thorough pass (the longer, the stronger or the best rung) reuses the facts the fast pass built (no second context build), widens the history to 8,000 tokens, sizes recall results 3,000 and opens 4,000 tokens (d1109-chat-recall's parameter), appends CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES to the system part, and has the fast pass's tools without answer_thoroughly (the same read, recall and command tools behind the registry's read-back; d1109-chat-guard's read-back after records applies), no web tools, the same token restrictions (allowedPaths [], allowedDomains [], autonomy as today); text the fast pass streamed before the hand-over is dropped (the step frame carries reset). CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES: "# Thinking it through\nThis question was handed to you to think through; the person waits and sees what you look up. Look up what the answer rests on with recall, recall_open and the read tools, a few lookups at most. Then answer in at most six short sentences, or a short list whose lines start with \"- \". Say what the answer rests on (sessions, tasks, cards, decisions or documents, by name and date), keep what the records say apart from what you conclude, and say what you could not check. When you suggest a next step, name one the app can do; make a change only when the person asked for it. When the app says to wrap up, answer from what you have." Why: one answer; nothing looked up twice, since the hand-over comes before any lookup.

The waiting line. POST /chat/stream sends 'turn' {turnId, startedAt} first, then 'step' {text, at, reset?} at each step, then tokens and the reply. The steps are d1109-chat-recall's stepLine words, plus the hand-over 'Thinking it through with Sonnet: about 20 seconds, at most CHF 0.30.' (the longer rung: 'Thinking it through more carefully: about 20 seconds, at most CHF 0.10.'), 'Answering with what I found…' at the wrap-up and 'Stopping…'. 'About N seconds' is the median of the last 20 thorough answers on that model in this install, rounded up to 10 s (30 with none; 'about a minute' from 55 s); the CHF is the pass's budget at the day's rate rounded up to the centime (the ask-above amount for a pass that goes ahead, the line's 'at most' after a yes). The UI shows 'Thinking…', then the newest step in the agent's bubble with ' · 7 s' from 3 s on, the reply streaming in its place; Send becomes Stop ('Stops this answer. Changes it already made stay, each with Undo.'); during a thorough pass Answer now sits beside Stop. The chat-stream client keeps ignoring frames it does not know, so the phone and older clients still get their reply. Why: the owner's indicator; code-written lines cannot carry injected text; design section 5 rules 1, 3, 6, 7, 9.

Turns in flight and Stop. The daemon keeps a registry of turns in flight (chat-turns.ts: turn id, human, conversation, step, since, depth, AbortController, the thorough budget's handle); its controller is passed with ChatRequest.signal to every driver run of the turn, which also makes voice's barge-in end the model call. POST /chat/turns/:id/stop (the turn's own human; another human 403 as notYourConversation; a finished turn answers {stopped: false}) aborts it: the run ends as killed, late usage is booked as today (R-lateusage), changes already made stay with their Undo, and the reply keeps its complete sentences and ends 'You stopped this answer: CHF 0.02 spent.' ('under CHF 0.01' below a centime). POST /chat/turns/:id/answer-now (a thorough pass only) makes its next call carry the wrap-up (SessionBudget.wrapUpNow, append-only). A dropped stream, a reload or closing Talk never stops a turn. Why: stopping is the person's; one conversation on several surfaces; nothing ends by accident.

Reload and restart. GET /projects/:id/conversation and GET /conversation serve answering {turnId, step, since, depth} for a turn in flight; /events emits conversation.changed {projectId} when a turn starts, at each new step and when it ends, and the UI re-reads the conversation on it. A person's line without a reply that is not in flight reads 'Forerunner closed before answering this.' when it is older than the daemon's start, else 'I could not answer this.'; both with Ask again, which sends the same line. Why: design section 1 (nothing stuck silently); true words for both causes.

After the answer. A longer or stronger reply has one muted line ('Thought it through with Sonnet · 34 s · CHF 0.06', 'Thought it through more carefully · 21 s · CHF 0.02') (under a centime 'under CHF 0.01'; on a Claude subscription 'on your Claude plan' in place of the CHF); a quick reply has none. A hand-over that waits for the person's yes leaves the ask line under the answer with Go ahead (the offer: its rung, its figures and the turn it answers, kept on the chat.reply row); under a longer answer that reached its wrap-up, the stronger rung's ask line with Go ahead, and under a stronger answer that reached its wrap-up, the best rung's when the project's highest model is above it ('This needs the strongest model: about CHF 0.60 (at most CHF 1.20) and 40 seconds. Go ahead?'); a refused one leaves 'This needs a closer look: about 20 seconds, about CHF 0.02.' with Think it through (the longer rung), or the cap line ('A closer look would pass this month's cap, so this is the quick answer.', 'A closer look would pass this project's budget, so this is the quick answer.', 'A closer look would pass the share of your Claude plan Forerunner may use, so this is the quick answer.'). The From line (d1109-chat-recall's sources, up to three records as links) under any reply that has them. Think it through under the newest model answer only, never under a command's sentence, a notice, a read-back, a voice turn or a thorough answer. chat.reply records depth, passes [{depth, model, effort, durationMs, costUsdMicro}], why, offer, stopped; ChatReplyView and ConversationTurnView gain footer, depth, offer, interrupted and failed, append-only. Why: transparency without noise (design section 3.9's must-not-show list, section 5 rule 5); 'at most' is a cap the code keeps, 'about' an estimate.

The setting chat_ask_above (global, per person, settings.set): the CHF above which one chat answer asks first, default CHF 0.10; 0 = chat asks before every longer answer; a stronger model always asks whatever the amount; a lower amount acts at once (narrowingActsAtOnce), a higher one is read back (medium risk), with Undo; display 'asks first above CHF 0.10' or 'asks before every longer answer'. Settings, Basics, one row beside the monthly cap: 'Chat asks first before a stronger model or an answer over CHF [0.10].' and 'Below that it thinks longer when it helps, on the same model.' (amounts with a point or a comma), and while chat runs on a Claude plan 'On your Claude plan the amount is counted at API prices.'. Why: the session lead's reading of the owner's answer 2 ('expensive: more than CHF 0.10 for one answer') as one number the person can move; the owner asked for no daily amount; Basics is where the money fields are (design section 6).

'# Now' gains thinking_longer: 'goes ahead up to CHF 0.10 on this model', 'asks the person first', 'not on a spoken turn' or 'not now (the caps leave too little)'. Why: the fast model rarely asks in vain; the line is volatile and uncached, so the cached prefix does not move.

Prompt caching: answer_thoroughly sits in the fast pass's tool list on every turn, in a fixed place after the recall tools, and is gated in code; nothing in the fast pass's tools, system or history depends on the gate; the thorough pass has its own model, system part and tool list and writes its own cache (about USD 0.02 on its first call, read by its later calls and by another thorough answer within 5 minutes), never touching the fast pass's entries. Why: R-chatcache.

Model-facing text is code, asserted verbatim on the requests: answer_thoroughly's definition "Hand this question to a stronger model that thinks it through and can look up more. It is slower (often half a minute) and costs more, within limits the app sets. Use it only when a good answer needs reasoning across many records (several sessions, tasks or days), working out why something keeps failing and what to change, a plan, a comparison, a review or a recommendation, or when the person asks you to think harder. Never for what is running, what is left, one record, a greeting or a change. Call it first, before any lookup, and write nothing before it. The app decides: it hands the question over, asks the person first, or tells you to answer from what you have. The facts' thinking_longer line says whether it is available now.", the refusal results, the ask result ('Not yet: the person is asked first. Answer in one or two sentences from what you have; the app adds the question under your answer.'), CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES, the chat wrap-up and conversation-agent.md 1.4.0's new section 'Thinking longer' (when to call answer_thoroughly, before any lookup, never for status, a record or a change; when the app says not now or not yet, answer briefly; under the 120-line rule).

Performance: a thorough reply is a chat_thorough sample measured on its total time and labelled 'Chat, thorough answers'; quick replies stay text_chat first-token samples. Why: a longer answer is no miss of the fast target.

[major] D1-15 (the owner's answer 1 of 2026-11-09, D9): a project already on this computer (made before the rule, or while GitHub could not be read) on a repository whose marker names a project another Forerunner uses is a second project of that repository with no way to become that project: d1109-onerepo-link's Overview line offers Take it over only when nobody else was active, and otherwise nothing. decisions: Shown, not stopped: each project of a set that shares a repository or folder (d1109-onerepo-link's index) gets one Overview line '"Site" and "Kite club" both work in o/site.' with Make one project; meanwhile both keep working as today and W15-01 keeps their pull requests apart. Why: keep today's behaviour where the owner did not decide (owner question 1 keeps the alternative).
The person picks the project to keep; no default is selected and the button stays disabled until one is. Why: 'without guessing'.

Command project.join {keep, close: [ids]} (new file packages/commands/src/commands/project-join.ts; risk medium, reversible; the dialog's press is the yes, chat reads it back with Yes and No). Only projects that share a repository or folder can be joined. Why: D1 only, no general merge of unrelated projects.

What moves, in one store transaction (SQLite and Postgres): the closing project's tasks of every status (ids, dependencies, branches, pr_url kept), its milestones after the kept project's (order_index offset), the cards about those tasks and its open cards, its queued notes, merge records, lessons, decisions and accepted source proposals; its data assets add the kept project to project_ids. What stays on the closing project, readable: sessions, cost-ledger rows, changes, chat and answered project cards. The closing project is archived with settings.joined_into {project, at}, its repos cleared and kept as settings.was_linked for Undo; the kept project's settings.joined_from gains its id. Why: the ledger is the truth caps are measured on and is never rewritten; history is not lost; task ids are what worktrees, branches and marks name, so nothing on disk or on GitHub has to change.

Open pull requests keep working: the moved tasks keep their pull requests and merge records; the kept project reads the closing project's id as its own in pull request marks and docs branches through d1109-onerepo-link's projectIdsOf, so the closing project's status, scaffold and intake docs pull requests are the kept one's (one status pull request again) and its task pull requests merge from the kept project's Overview. Nothing on GitHub is edited. A join into a together project (OJ-11) is the exception to this decision: the together rule wins over joined_from there, and OJ-11 says what happens to the closing project's docs and status pull requests. Why: no write to GitHub for a local reorganisation.

Refused in words, with the button disabled, while: a session runs on either project ('A session is working on "Kite club". Make one project when it ends.'); a plan card of a closing project is open ('The plan of "Kite club" waits for your answer. Answer it first.'); a merge of one of its pull requests is in flight ('A pull request of "Kite club" is being merged. Try again in a minute.'); a session of either project waits to go on after a Claude credential wait, a start is kept for a credential's reset or a hands-off start is held ('A session of "Kite club" waits to go on at 15:40. Make one project after it ran, or cancel it first.'), since the closed project's continuation or kept start would otherwise be dropped without a word while its tasks still read '...; then your session goes on.'; the projects share no repository or folder. Why: no row moves under a running worker, and nothing the person was told will go on is silently dropped.

Settings: the kept project's settings apply to the moved work; the dialog names each that differs in one line (budget per session, project budget, who merges, what research reads), e.g. 'Who merges: "Site"'s setting applies to the moved work: you press Merge.' Why: no silent change of a limit or a rule; the person sees it before pressing.

Money: no cap, budget or ledger row changes; the kept project's cap keeps measuring its own ledger; the closing project's spend stays booked to it and shows on the kept project's Costs as 'Spent in "Kite club" before it joined: CHF 3.20'. Why: no budget is passed and spend stays visible in CHF.

The closed project's page: status sentence 'Joined into "Site" on 9 Nov.' with Open it, no Start or New task (ProjectPage.tsx's joined branch beside w15-tail's removed one: a joined project never reads 'This project was removed.'); its sessions, changes, costs and chat remain readable; the kept project's Overview says 'Includes the work of "Kite club".' linking to it; Home lists only the kept project; d1109-onerepo-link's index counts it as the kept project, never as removed. Why: history stays one click away, in true words.

Undo (Changes): moves every moved row back (and rows made on the kept project since for a moved task, such as a card), and a moved task merged from the kept project since moves back with its merge record; reopens the closing project with its link and removes it from joined_from; refused in words while a session runs on the kept project, a moved task's merge is in flight, or a task of the kept project that was not moved waits for a moved task ('"Shop page" waits for "Cart", which came from "Kite club": change that first.'); works after a restart. Why: a safe way is a reversible one, and Undo never leaves a dependency across two projects.

Removing the kept project: Undo of its project.create is refused while settings.joined_from is not empty ('This project includes the work of "Kite club", so its creation cannot be undone.'), beside w15-tail's refusal while a session runs. Why: undoing it would archive the kept project with the closed project's moved tasks inside.

The joined project in the Sessions list and in chat: rows stay where they are (no session or ledger row moves), so the kept project's Sessions list (d1109-sessions) ends with one line '"Kite club" had 3 sessions before it joined.' with Open (the closed project's Sessions list); chat's scope (d1109-chat-guard's scopeOf) includes the projects joined into the asked one through d1109-onerepo-link's projectIdsOf, so recall finds the closed project's records from the kept project, each named as "Kite club"'s. Why: the adversarial check found the two designs' handoffs contradicted each other and neither built it; one rule (nothing moves, the kept project links and reads) keeps the ledger whole.

Archiving is used here only for a join: the closed project is archived with joined_into, readable, never deleted. W5-40 (removing a project: none, archive or delete) stays open for every other case; ADR 0117 says so.

Work together for a project already here (OJ-11, D9): on d1109-onerepo-link's Overview line 'o/kite is also the Forerunner project "Kite club", which is not on this computer.', when the repository names exactly one such project, Work together opens JoinProjectsDialog in its together form: '"Site" becomes "Kite club", the project GitHub knows: its tasks, plan and cards move into it, and this Forerunner works on it together with the other one.' (one sentence of what moves, the settings lines as for every join). project.join {keep: {together: true}, close: [Site]} makes, in the same store transaction, the together project with the repository's id and name (d1109-onerepo-link's Work together decision: read from the repository at the press; no marker, scaffold, docs or status pull request of that id) and moves Site's work into it as OJ-02 moves it; Site is closed into it (joined_into) and its id goes into the kept project's joined_from; the together rule wins over joined_from: the together project writes no status and no docs pull request, Site's included, because fr/status is one branch per repository (docs.ts STATUS_BRANCH) and, while this install kept writing Site's status there, the other Forerunner, whose project the marker names, would keep its own status in the app ('while another project's status pull request is open'), and this Forerunner's Docs row would be untrue. So the join closes Site's own open status pull request (marked with Site's id, opened by this install; never one with another id or none) through the host's updatePullRequest after the store transaction, the one GitHub write of a join into a together project, said in the dialog ('This closes "Site"'s status pull request #12 on GitHub; this Forerunner then keeps the status in the app.'; if GitHub refuses the close, the join stands and the Overview says once 'Close "Site"'s status pull request #12 on GitHub: while it is open, the status of "Kite club" cannot go there.'); Site's open docs pull requests (its intake docs branch, its scaffold) stay on GitHub as they are and are listed on the together project's Overview as information, with no Merge and never written to ('From "Site" before you worked on "Kite club" together: close it on GitHub if it is not needed.'); the other Forerunner's pull requests are never touched. Refusals: OJ's, plus the repository naming another project or none at the press, and GitHub not readable ('GitHub did not answer, so the project cannot be checked. Try again.'). Undo as OJ-04 (Site reopened with its link and its rows back, the together row removed; its status pull request stays closed on GitHub, said once: 'Its status pull request stays closed on GitHub; with Status pull request on, its next session opens one again.'). When one of a pair here (made before the rule) is a together project, the dialog keeps it ('"Kite club" is the project GitHub knows, so it is kept.'). Why: the owner's answer 1: a second project of a repository another Forerunner works on becomes that project without a take-over; the join's one transaction and its Undo already do the moving; one repository has one status branch, and it now belongs to the project both Forerunners work on, so this Forerunner's old one is closed rather than kept.

problems: [major] D7-1: After the plan is approved the agent never corrects its own task list: a task a specialist finds is two jobs, a missing step, a wrong order or a duplicate stays as planned; the person edits each task by hand or redrafts the whole plan. Owner's words: "if I say set this up and I approve a plan and then it adds a bunch of tasks, I want it to be able to fix its tasks. Like as part of a run, it should be able to do things like that." Where: session/runner.ts:1379-1476 (replan only takes tasks that became ready), :3825-3858 (StaticPlanner, no model call), daemon/compose.ts:2675.

[major] D7-2: A specialist that finds its task too big, a step missing or a wrong order has nowhere to say so that anything reads; rung 2 of the ladder asks it to 'say in the report what should be split off' and nothing reads it, and the ladder's split is not built (only 'change specialist'). Owner's words: "I want it to be able to fix its tasks." Where: session/executor.ts:640-641, :784-800 (ladderStandIn), :1013 (the report's only headings), models/ladder.ts:305.

[major] D7-4: The autonomy level cannot decide when the agent asks first about its tasks: creating or editing tasks is 'non_routine', free only from Trusted, and no class covers the agent's own fixes. Owner's words: "The agent changing its own tasks with the autonomy level deciding when it asks first. That's also good." Where: enforcement/autonomy.ts:36-49, :64-74.

[major] D7-3a: The task commands cannot express the fixes: no split, no 'add a step before X', no 'drop as a duplicate'; cancel is always medium risk. Owner's words: "I want it to be able to fix its tasks." Where: packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:835-950 (task.create), :960-1027 (task.transition, :965), types.ts:33-60 (COMMAND_NAMES).

decisions: The check runs on evidence only (a report's 'For the task list:' lines, a review note the task did not cause, notes kept from before), at most once per task boundary and three times a session, never after the wrap-up line. Why: cost; the owner wants fixes 'as part of a run', not a paid replan after every task.

The planning model at one effort step below the intake (medium), 4,096 output tokens, 120 s, a JSON reply and no tools, routed like the intake's planning call, capped at its own estimate inside the session's work budget, a Run row 'task-check' booked in the session. Why: planning quality for a small call; one path on both credentials; money visible and inside the budget.

Five kinds of change, each a registry command (task.update, task.dependencies, task.create with 'then', task.split, task.transition with 'duplicate_of'). Why: every change gets the change log, the version check and a state-based Undo that survives a restart (ADR 0030); no new write path to the store.

A split keeps the task as its first part and adds 1 to 3 new tasks; every criterion goes word for word into a part; a task's own budget is shared, never raised. Why: the folder, branch and earlier work stay; the bar cannot be lowered by splitting; no budget is passed.

New action class plan_fix, free from Standard up (Standard, Trusted, Autopilot); Advisor and Assisted get one suggestion card. Why: the owner confirmed on 2026-11-09 that the agent changes its own tasks without asking from Standard up and asks first at Advisor and Assisted on one card (the autonomy level deciding when it asks first); plan_fix frees only the bounded fixes.

Ask first at every level for flagged input, the person's own task, a criterion removed from a task that ran or has open findings, a deploy or migration step, a question for the person, a new task whose specialist reaches further than its source task's, more than two drops, or an unlike duplicate. Why: these are the changes whose mistake costs the person (their edit lost, the bar lowered, risky work or their time added, work cancelled).

Each change the agent makes alone is one Changes row (source 'session') with one Undo, a line on the session page and no Inbox line; the session's one Update counts them. A set the person approves with one Yes is one row with one Undo. Why: the confirmed 'every change shown with one Undo' and design §3.8's 'What becomes an Update: one line per session'.

Added work joins the running session only by d1109-starts-engine's admit rule: the parts of a split promised task share its remaining estimate, a new task or a step before a promised task joins only if the room after the promise and what joined covers it (else both wait for the next Start, named once), and the check itself is paid only from that room; the agent's preparation never starts a session, the hands-off setting included. Why: D6 (the person says when a session starts) and option C ('the session keeps its promise').

A task with an open card (failed after its tries, needs your answer, paused at a budget) or paused by the person is left alone. Why: the card is the one place for that decision (design §3.8); D4's continuation stays as built.

Evidence goes in the data envelope and is scanned; a flagged line is kept, never sent to the model, and turns the set into a suggestion card that quotes it; a new task's specialist reaches no further than its source task's without a yes; a task written from a report says so in its brief; the strict schema and the fence hold whatever the model returns; the check's run has no tools. Why: a prompt may ask, only code can allow (AGENTS.md); a report must not reach the web through a task it wrote.

decisions: CE-1 One policy: human.notify_prefs.credential_policy, one of subscription_then_wait, subscription_then_ask, subscription_then_key, key_then_subscription, key_only (packages/billing/src/policy.ts: CREDENTIAL_POLICIES; ruleOf(id) = {order, whenStopped: next | ask | wait, kinds}, key_only without the subscription; credentialPolicyOf(prefs) = the stored id, else derived at every read: billing_order with the subscription first + wait or unset -> subscription_then_wait, + use_other -> subscription_then_key, api_key or plan_credits first + use_other -> key_then_subscription, + wait or unset -> {chosen: 'earlier', the stored order, whenStopped wait, both kinds: the chooser keeps running a task only the subscription can do here on it, as today, which key_only would not}, no billing_order -> the default preset subscription_then_wait for every call and every purpose ({chosen: false}, so Settings shows it as used until the person picks), or subscription_then_key under an explicit mid_session_limit use_other; CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER, the routed provider's fallbackOrder and every other per-call order go: one order for tasks, chat, planning, reviews, the task check and the background jobs (the chooser's capability moves stay, said on the plan card, ADR 0100 point 13); stopKeyOf(source, status); moneyRank, the earlier choice ranked as key_only). Why: the owner's 'a framework for what to use when, and then the system just does it'; read at every pick, so a change applies to the next call; deriving at read changes nothing a person chose (an explicit earlier choice is kept as it was chosen), and a person who never chose gets the default preset for everything, not a hidden split (the owner's answer 4 of 2026-11-09: 'it should use the order that the user specifies ... There should be a nice clean options menu'; ADR 0100 point 2 amended).

CE-2 The router holds every stop: RouteContext.whenStopped replaces waitOnRest (waitOnRest still read as 'wait' for one release); the held list covers resting (reason limit), refused, plan_share (share, until the next month's start UTC) and monthly_limit (key_month), each with until and stopKey; under ask and wait a held first choice throws unavailable with details.waitFor {sourceId, kind, reason, until, stopKey, ask}; a grant {to, stopKey} on the held source whose stopKey is the current one lets the granted kind serve; a grant never lifts the hold for purpose batch (background jobs); next moves as today; RouteContext.heldNow (sources the caller saw stop on this call) are held like resting ones. Why: one place decides, so every caller agrees (7a, 7b, 7c).

CE-3 RouterTaskBilling.pick reads the policy at every pick for every purpose (session, critic, interactive, which D7's task check uses, chat, batch; a grant covers every purpose but batch); the sources in req.exclude go to the router as heldNow, not as withheld, under ask and wait; at a stop it never moves to a lower chooser group: the task waits with reason needs. The agent's task check (d1109-selftasks-run's runTaskCheck, merged in C4) is held like planning: under wait or an unanswered ask it makes no call, books nothing, keeps its notes for the next boundary or session and returns held with the wait (this area's one branch in task-check.ts); under ask its hold ensures the one ask card (CE-7). Why: one rule for every call; the exclude list today hides the very stop the hold must see; the plan card's 'only it can' stays true (ADR 0100 point 13).

CE-4 RoutedProvider follows the rule and has no order of its own (its fallbackOrder, CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER, goes: the policy's order for every call): after rest or refuse it picks again under the rule; under ask and wait the call ends with the wait (code unavailable, details.wait), which each caller handles as today: the critic's review waits in review without a counted try (review-refusal.ts), the plan waits (the intake's waitNow), chat holds (CE-9), a job skips (CE-10); under next one move as today, recorded with its cost (CE-11). holdNow(model) beside waitNow says whether a call would be held and whether a one-off switch could serve (for chat and d1109-chat-depth's thorough pass). Why: D5-1 is the main money leak today.

CE-5 A task its credential stopped keeps its work; under next, or after a grant, it goes back to the head of the session's queue and continues on the next credential in the same session; the brief's previous-run section for a usage_limit, credential_refused or share-stopped run is a sibling of whereTheLastRunStopped with exact text ('stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit' / 'was refused' / 'reached the share of the subscription Forerunner may use'), never 'It failed', with its siblings for a run that changed no file ('The last run of this task stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit, before it changed any file.') and for one that left no note ('It left no note: its Claude credential stopped it before it could write one.'); under ask and wait it waits, the session goes on with what can run and ends to wait, and at the stop's end that session goes on by itself as the person's own start (d1109-starts-engine S-10's continuation: the rest of its promise and budget, on the credential that is back, never another one unless the rule is next or a grant of this stop covers it), while work outside a session the person started is ready for the person's next Start. Why: 7a ('the task to be completed by the API') without spending twice.

CE-6 Forerunner's share reached mid-run (the hooks' plan level, unchanged) returns as a credential stop with reason share and its handoff kept on the run (read by CE-5's brief): no budget card, the session does not end for it, the rule decides; the stop ends at the month's start or when the person raises the allowance (the share falls under the cap; the stop key changes); then a person's session that waited for it goes on by itself (d1109-starts-engine S-10's continuation, on the subscription) and other waiting work reads Ready for the next Start; nothing else starts (d1109-starts-engine S-3, S-10). The raise's change line is this area's (it replaces S-3's line for the allowance): with a person's session waiting on the share 'Your subscription's allowance is raised: your session of 14:05 goes on now.' (inside quiet hours '... goes on at 07:00, after your quiet hours.'), otherwise 'Your subscription's allowance is raised: 2 tasks are ready again for your next Start.'. The ask card's Wait line for the share has CE-7's two forms: 'Nothing moves until Tue 1 Dec, 01:00, or until you raise the allowance; then your session goes on.' while the person's session waits, else 'Nothing moves. After Tue 1 Dec, 01:00, or a raised allowance, the work runs at your next Start.' (the month's start UTC shown in the person's time zone). Budget cards at source 'plan' filed before the upgrade keep their wake (wakeBudgetWaits). Why: one behaviour per stop; a raised allowance must end the wait (U-052); no limit passed.

CE-7 Ask first: one card per stop (key credential:ask), filed only by the writer that set limits.asking {stopKey, requestId} with the version check, only when work needs it (a task run, a review, planning, the task check; not chat alone, not a job), the other credential can serve now and the caps have room for the waiting work's next call; its words from credential-words.ts, computed when shown. 'Use API key' re-reads the stop, writes limits.grant {to, stopKey, by: 'card', at} (version-checked; audit billing.grant), then: the waiting tasks of a session that still runs go back into it as its own tasks (d1109-starts-engine's readmit on the admit handle, which clears the runner's notAgain for them), a session that ended to wait goes on now as the person's start (personContinue: by 'person', the rest of its promise, its cap less what the ledger booked), a waiting plan is drafted, work outside a person's session stays ready for the next Start. The grant covers every project's tasks, their reviews and planning, the task check and chat until the stop ends (the owner's answer 3: 'For all work.'); Forerunner's own monthly checks (the model watch and the critic's check on known examples, CE-10) are not the person's work and wait for the first choice at no cost; the option's consequence line says what the yes covers ('Your work and chat use your API key until 15:40: about CHF 0.90 for what waits now.') and the card's Details says the rest once ('Forerunner's own monthly checks wait for your subscription; they cost nothing meanwhile.'). 'Wait' closes the card and moves nothing until the stop ends; then the person's waiting session goes on by itself on the first choice (its continuation stays kept: 'Nothing moves until 15:40; then your session goes on with your subscription.'), and work outside a person's session is ready for the next Start ('Nothing moves. After 15:40 the work runs at your next Start.' when no session of the person waits); the asking mark keeps the stop, so no second card comes; the time a Wait line names is when the session goes on: the stop's end, or the end of the person's quiet hours when that is later (d1109-starts-engine S-10); recordWait(source, stopKey) records the same answer without a card, for the Start dialog's 'Start at 15:40' under ask (d1109-cred-screens), so no card follows the person's own choice. A second or late answer changes nothing and returns the card's Done line; an answer after the stop ended grants nothing. The wake, before takeReady, ends grants whose stop is over and withdraws open cards whose stop ended (then the waiting session goes on as after Wait), whose other credential cannot serve any more, or whose preset changed. Why: 'after asking human' as one card; answered once; restart-safe; no start the person did not ask for (D6).

CE-8 A refusal follows the rule and always informs: one card per refusal at a time, filed only by the writer that flips limits.refusedCard {refusedAt, open} to open with the version check (refuse() and noteWait's TR-10 path alike: concurrent refusals file one, and work that waits on the still-refused credential after the card was closed files it once more); closing the card clears open; refusalWhyOf(error) stores a category (expired sign-in, invalid or deleted key, not allowed for this model or workspace, other), never the provider's text; the card's body says what the work does under the rule (wait, next, or ask with Use API key / Wait, staying open as the fix-it card after an answer); a refused credential gets no second request from any path (a switch, a grant, a continuation, a late answer, chat, a job, the probe) until a different one is saved. Why: 7c; no retry that could lock the person's account.

CE-9 Chat asks holdNow before its model path; held: no model call and no ledger row, the hold reply written by code, with a per-turn 'Use API key' when the other credential serves now and the caps have room (the reply view's oneOff {label, explain}; the press runs that one question again with allowSwitch on that request only: no grant, no card; the route's flag for the press is d1109-cred-screens'); a standing grant or next: chat answers on the other credential and the reply's note says so once per stop per conversation; 'I could not answer (' never appears for a credential wait. Why: chat spends too (7b); the smallest consent; the person is in the chat. Under the default preset (nothing chosen) chat answers on the subscription too (one order, the owner's answer 4), so at the subscription's limit under its wait chat holds as above, with the one-off press; d1109-chat-depth's ask line, hand-over step, footer, setting row and Think it through then use their Claude-plan forms (the amounts at API prices, 'on your Claude plan'; built here if C3 left that wording in not_done); a longer pass that goes ahead without asking runs on the credential the policy serves chat now, and the ask line names that credential when it is not the person's first (d1109-chat-depth's first-credential check is replaced by this).

CE-10 Background jobs (batch: the model watch and its evals, the monthly calibration) never ask and never switch under ask or wait, a standing grant included: a held call spends nothing, files no card, logs one line, and the job is not marked done for its period, so the first tick after the stop runs it. Why: no card and no money for work nobody started.

CE-11 Switch data: the run row's artifacts carry switchedFrom {kind, stop}; the session log gets billing.switch {taskId, from, to, stop, until} once per stop and billing.back once when the first choice serves again; SessionResult.switched [{taskId, from, to, usdMicro}] summed from the ledger; CostView.byCredential (each billing source's spend in the view's window); RoutedProvider's fallback sentence in the person's time zone; the log lines from credential-words.ts. Why: every screen (d1109-cred-screens) reads data, not re-parsed sentences; 7a 'transparent'.

CE-12 One notification (credentialSwitched, normal urgency) per stop and session, only for a move onto money the policy made by itself inside a running session: not for a grant the person gave, not for a session whose Start dialog said it would run on the key, not for a move onto the subscription; deduplicated by limits.switchNotified {stopKey, sessionIds} (version-checked, restart-safe); none for a wait. Why: 7a and 7c ('notification or information'); the owner wants no notifications about waiting work.

CE-13 settings.set credential_policy: medium risk; narrows by moneyRank (subscription_then_wait 0, subscription_then_ask 1, subscription_then_key 2, key_then_subscription 3, key_only 3; not chosen counts as the preset it reads as: the default subscription_then_wait 0, or subscription_then_key 2 under an explicit use_other), so a narrowing acts at once and a widening asks the person's yes; an agent actor is refused; an Undo is judged the same way; the settings_set tool definition lists credential_policy with its five values and neither legacy key; settings.set billing_order or mid_session_limit once credential_policy is stored, and an Undo of their old rows, answer 'This was replaced by "Which Claude does the work"; change it there.'. Why: money settings never widen by text; a tool definition is model-facing code.
root_causes: packages/billing/src/router.ts: the 'wait' rule (waitOnRest) was built for task runs and two kinds of stop (a rest, a refusal); the share and the key's monthly cap stayed plain skips, so they move work onto the next credential under any setting.

packages/runtime/src/wiring/billing-pick.ts: the sources a caller saw stop on this call are withheld before the router (exclude), and the groups loop moves to a lower chooser group on any 'no source' that is not a hold.

packages/runtime/src/provider/routed.ts: the non-task calls have their own one-time move to the next source, outside the person's setting, and their own fallback order (CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER) for a person who chose none.

packages/runtime/src/session/billing.ts and packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts: an order and a mid-session rule as two settings with different reach per purpose; no value for asking and no state for an answer (asked, granted).
packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts and budget-pause.ts: the subscription's share is enforced as a money budget level and handled as a budget pause, not as the subscription running out.
packages/runtime/src/session/task-context.ts: a credential-stopped run is read as a failed attempt although its work is kept.
packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts, routed.ts and notifications/producers.ts: a switch is a log sentence only; no fact on the run, the session or the result, no producer.
packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts and billing-pick.ts refuse(): filing a card is not tied to the version-checked mark that decided it, and the card stores no reason.

problems: [major] D8-1: The header's running chip names the task but not the project while a task runs, only the project between tasks, during the critic's review and while the session plans, nothing for a session that waits to go on, and has no Stop; Owner's words: "it should at least be very clear to a user when a run is ongoing. That should also be very visually clear no matter where the person is."; Where: apps/ui/src/shell/ShellBars.tsx:49-73 (RunningChip), packages/runtime/src/daemon/project-status.ts:446-484 (workingOn reads the session's whole event list for task.started only).

That should also be very visually clear no matter where the person is."; Where: apps/ui/src/components/Dialog.tsx:4, :29 (showModal), apps/ui/src/shell/ConversationPanel.tsx:690.

That should also be very visually clear no matter where the person is."; Where: ShellBars.tsx:80-154, apps/ui/src/shell/Shell.tsx:349 and :381, apps/ui/src/pages/HomePage.tsx:188-225, apps/ui/src/pages/project/SummaryTab.tsx:102-130.
