[minor] D8-6: A session that ended to wait for a Claude credential offers no way to go on with what is left of its budget, and a start the person keeps for the reset (d1109-starts-engine S-10) would be shown nowhere, so the person could not tell that something will start at 15:40 or stop it; Owner's words: "It should definitely not automatically do something even when told to wait or showing that it is waiting."; Where: project-status.ts:279-296; apps/ui/src/pages/SessionPage.tsx (no Continue for a session that ended to wait). The owner decided on 2026-11-09 that such a session goes on by itself when the credential is back, 'shown on the run indicator while it waits ("Waiting until 15:40, then it goes on", with Cancel)'.

[minor] D8-7: With only the person's Start starting work, ready work must be offered plainly: the project line reads 'Ready to continue: 3 tasks ready', an answer's Done line offers nothing, and a person's start waiting behind another project's session is said nowhere on the project; Owner's words: "the user clearly states when a session will run"; Where: project-status.ts:298-317, apps/ui/src/pages/InboxPage.tsx:497-511 and :748.
decisions: V-1 One run state in the daemon's words: a new daemon/run-indicator.ts computes RunningView[] ({sessionId, projectId, projectName, state, text, since, stop: ['after','now','all'], then?}) from the active sessions (not the chat's conversation row, not a plan being drafted; the critic's monthly calibration, a session on no project, is shown, D8: 'Forerunner · the critic's monthly check on known examples' with Stop now and Stop all, and in the indicator's open form (the Stop menu's head, the Talk panel's line and the tray's tooltip) one sentence of what it does, in the form of the credential its running call uses (the Run row's billing source): on the API key 'Once a month the critic reviews examples whose right answers are known, so you see whether it still catches mistakes; it spends at most CHF 8.00 a month of its own budget.', on the Claude plan 'Once a month the critic reviews examples whose right answers are known, so you see whether it still catches mistakes; it runs on your Claude plan, within CHF 8.00 a month at API prices.' (the figure: the calibration's monthly budget at the day's rate; design §5 rule 6: plain words, no 'verdict'; the owner's answer 6 of 2026-11-09 asked what it is for), their last task, review and stop events, the scheduler's waiting person starts and the person's sessions waiting to go on after a credential wait (the kept continuation on a wait entry, d1109-starts-engine S-10: state 'waiting', no stop choices, cancel true); GET /running answers it, a run.changed event carries it on the stream and in polling, and /health gains running {projectName, text} (append-only) while activeSessions stops counting a plan being drafted. The words: 'Quote page · the coder works on "Style the page"', '... · the critic checks "X"', '... · picks the next task', '... · plans the session', '... · wraps up "X" at its budget', '... · stops after "X"', '· then Garden site' for a waiting person start; 'Quote page · waiting until 15:40, then it goes on' for a person's session waiting for its Claude credential (the owner's words of 2026-11-09; 'Quote page · waiting for a new API key, then it goes on' after a refusal; when the person's quiet hours end later than the stop, their end: 'Quote page · waiting until 07:00 (after your quiet hours), then it goes on'; a wait for any other reason, such as the share or a key's monthly cap that d1109-cred-engine adds beside this area, the generic 'Quote page · waiting for Claude, then it goes on', which d1109-cred-screens words with its date in C6); each at most 80 characters with titles shortened. runText is exported so d1109-sessions' working row says the same words. Why: one place per fact (design §5 rule 10); the phone later shows the same words (ADR 0102); the shell needs it without the UI.

V-2 One element on every page: RunIndicator, a bar directly under the header (role status, a pulsing dot, the words, the elapsed time, Stop ▾) on every route and at every width, never inside the collapsed menu, replacing RunningChip and the header's Stop all button; Stop offers Stop after this task (POST /sessions/:id/pause), Stop now (POST /sessions/:id/stop, asked once) and Stop all (POST /kill, asked once, 'Stops every session; none starts until you allow it again.'); the text opens the session; the store keeps it from run.changed; document.title reads '● Quote page · Forerunner' while it runs. The stopped bar, the no-key bar and the palette's Stop all question stay. Why: the owner: 'very visually clear no matter where the person is'; 'no clutter': one consistent element instead of two. A waiting session's bar shows its words (V-1's, e.g. 'Quote page · waiting until 15:40, then it goes on') with Cancel in place of Stop, without the pulsing dot; Cancel's one-line explanation is 'Nothing starts when Claude is back; its tasks wait for your Start.' and it sends POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel; document.title changes only while a session runs.

V-3 The same element elsewhere: Home's and the Overview's Working now render RunIndicator in its block form (same words, same Stop), and the project status line (project-status.ts, design §2) adds 'Waiting until 15:40 (your subscription's limit), then it goes on' with Cancel (the person's session waiting to go on), 'Starts at 15:40 (your subscription's limit)' with Cancel (a start kept for a reset, POST /projects/:id/continuation/cancel), 'Starts after your quiet hours' (a held hands-off start) and 'Starts after the session on "Quote page"' (a waiting person start), and rule 4 reads 'Ready: 3 tasks wait for your Start' with Continue. Why: design §3.2 and §3.4 keep Working now; the owner named 'Home, the project'; the project's one sentence says what waits and what will start.
V-4 Talk shows it: the conversation panel's first line is RunIndicator's compact form with Stop. Why: the modal covers the header.

V-5 The ended session's page says what comes next: a session that ended to wait for its credential with its continuation kept shows one block 'Waiting until 15:40 (your subscription's limit), then it goes on with "B" and 1 more.' with Cancel; after Cancel (or when no continuation is kept) 'Stopped to wait for your subscription's limit until 15:40: "B" and 1 more wait.' with Continue ('Opens Start with the rest of this session and the CHF 1.20 left of its budget.'); with a person start kept for the reset instead, 'Starts again at 15:40 with "B" and 1 more.' with Cancel. Why: the owner's decision of 2026-11-09 (the person's session goes on by itself, shown with Cancel); the person who opens that session can stop the wait or go on with what is left.

V-6 The Inbox's Done line offers Start when the answer prepared work and no session of that project runs (it opens that project's Start dialog); never while one runs. Why: the person's start is one click from where they answered, without a reminder.

V-7 The desktop shell: tray_view's tooltip starts with /health.running ('Quote page: the coder works on "A"'), the tray menu's first item shows the same words (disabled) while a session runs, 'Stop all sessions' and 'Allow sessions again' replace 'Kill switch: stop everything' and 'Resume' (the question 'Stop every running session now? No session starts until you allow it again.'), and the main window's title is 'Forerunner — Quote page is working' while one runs, 'Forerunner' otherwise. Why: a minimised window or the tray is where a person looks when the window is not on screen; design §5 plain words. While a person's session only waits to go on, the tooltip's first line and the menu's first item read 'Quote page: waiting until 15:40, then it goes on' and the title and the icon stay as when nothing runs (the dot and the title mean a session runs now).
V-8 The tray icon gets a blue dot while a session runs, drawn over the app's own icon at run time (no new asset). Why: the one signal visible without hovering, on Windows and Linux.
V-9 Docs and the bench walk with screenshots of every screen with and without a running session.

areas.title: The policy where the person reads it: Settings -> Basics 'Which Claude does the work', one clean options menu (five presets whose labels show the order, the default marked as used until the person picks, each credential's role and state now, one line of what happens next) replacing Advanced's order list and the mid-session row; one line in the Start dialog and on the plan card, with 'Use API key' / 'Start at 15:40' in the dialog when the first choice is out; every stop and the open question in rows and the project status; the switch on the session page, the task drawer, the run indicator and Costs; the ask and refused cards and chat's one-off press on screen

Owner's words: "It should also be possible to give a framework for what to use when, and then the system just does it. e.g. use subscription until runs out --> go to API automatically, or use use subscription until runs out --> go to API after asking human, or go to API by default". decisions: CS-1 One section in Basics, 'Which Claude does the work', right under Accounts and keys, from GET /settings/credential-policy (CredentialPolicyView built by credential-policy-view.ts: the five presets with label, line and whether they move to money without asking; the rows in order with name, role, state words, the month's spend and a link; the now line; the runs-out line; the footnote; the one-credential sentence; the not-chosen state (the default preset 'Subscription first, then wait' selected and marked 'Used until you choose: your subscription first for everything it can do here; when it runs out, the work waits.' (a task only the API key can do here runs on it, as its plan card says, ADR 0100 point 13)); the earlier-choice line for an earlier key-first order with wait; a standing grant); a choice goes through POST /commands/execute settings.set credential_policy and its change card, so Changes and Undo work as for every row; 'Stop using it' on a standing grant calls POST /settings/credential-policy/grant/end (the engine's endGrant). Why: one place, read once; no new write route for the choice; the owner's answer 4 of 2026-11-09: 'the order that the user specifies ... a nice clean options menu', one order for every call, the default until the person picks, no hidden split.

CS-2 Advanced loses 'Claude: which to use first' (Move up / Move down) and the 'When my first choice runs out mid-session' row; it keeps 'What each can do here' (AbilityTable), the subscription allowance and 'Code tasks that need commands'; ADVANCED_CONTENTS says 'what each Claude credential can do here, the subscription allowance'. GET /settings/billing-order keeps answering and POST maps onto the policy (the order changed, the rule kept). Why: no two places for one fact (design section 5 rule 10).

CS-3 The Start dialog shows one line under the plan sentence (ifRunsOutLine; none with one credential); with the first choice stopped: under next the run-out line; under ask and wait two buttons, 'Use API key' (POST /sessions with useOtherCredential: true: the engine's grant writer, an open ask card closed with its Done line, a person start) and 'Start at 15:40' (a person start kept on the wait entry and made once at the reset, d1109-starts-engine's keepStartAtReset; the project then says 'Starts at 15:40 (your subscription's limit)' with Cancel; under ask it also records the person's Wait for this stop, so no card follows), offered only when no session of the project already waits to go on: when one does, the dialog says 'Your session of 14:05 goes on by itself at 15:40.' instead of 'Start at 15:40' and Start (d1109-starts-engine's one wait per project: a Start then keeps and starts nothing), and 'Use API key' continues that session now on the key (the time in 'goes on by itself at' is the later of the reset and the end of the person's quiet hours); the button the preset leans to comes first; neither when the other credential cannot serve or the caps have no room; with a yes standing, one line 'You said yes to your API key until 15:40, so this runs on it (about CHF 0.90).' and no buttons. Why: the person is there; 'wait' means the app does nothing by itself, not that the person cannot choose (owner question).
CS-4 The plan card shows the same line once at its foot, computed when shown. Why: the plan card is where the person approves money.

CS-5 Rows and the project status say every stop and the question: share ('Waits until Tue 1 Dec (your subscription's share)' [Change the allowance] -> /settings#plan-allowance), key_month, needs ('Waits for your API key: only it can read web pages here.'), the ask ('Waits for your answer: use your API key?' [Answer]; status rule 1 'Waiting for you: use your API key?'), with d1109-starts-engine's after-the-wait clause. Why: design section 1 'nothing is stuck silently'.

CS-6 The session page's switch log lines (billing.switch, billing.back), one line under its spend after a switch, the result's switch line, and the task drawer's run line, all from the engine's data. Why: 7a 'transparent' on the task and the session.

CS-7 The run indicator adds ' on your API key' after the task while the running task is on the credential the preset puts second, and ' · 1 task waits for your answer' with Answer (opening the card) while a task of the running session waits on an open ask card; a person's session waiting to go on is in the indicator as d1109-run-visible shows it ('Quote page · waiting until 15:40, then it goes on' with Cancel), and while its ask card is open the bar also offers Answer (opening the card); this area words the waits d1109-run-visible shows in its generic form: the share ('Quote page · waiting until Tue 1 Dec, 01:00, then it goes on' with Cancel and Change the allowance) and a key's monthly cap ('Quote page · waiting until Tue 1 Dec, 01:00 (your API key's monthly cap), then it goes on' with Cancel), on the indicator, the project status line's rule 2 and the session page's ended-to-wait block, the date and time in the person's time zone (the stop ends at the month's start UTC) or the end of the quiet hours when later; the project's status line 'Waiting for you: use your API key?' says it too (CS-5). Why: D8 'what it is doing', 7a.

CS-8 The Inbox shows the ask card and the refused card as every card (title, body, options with their consequence lines, the link), the preset's lean primary; the same card component inline where chat refers to it; chat's hold reply shows its one-off 'Use API key' with its line (the reply view's oneOff), sent as POST /chat's one-off flag, disabled after the press until the answer arrives. Why: design section 3.8 and 3.9.
CS-9 Costs gains 'By credential' (your API key in CHF; your subscription as its estimate and its share of the allowance) from CostView.byCredential. Why: 7a: the spend shows the switch.
CS-10 A bench walk before and after with screenshots of every screen above under each preset. Why: design section 7: a fix is done when the journey matches the design on the bench.

Then the siblings (validation rule 8: every screen that names a credential or its wait: Settings, the Start dialog, the plan card, New task's runs-on line, the Tasks row and drawer, the Overview, Home, the session page, the run indicator, chat, Costs). Restart: the section after composing the daemon twice shows the stored or derived choice; the Start dialog's 'Use API key' grant still stands after a restart until the stop ends; an Undo of a preset after a restart. Words: the screens' sentences only from credential-policy-view.ts (this area) and the cards' and log lines from credential-words.ts (d1109-cred-engine; a sentence missing there is listed in new_problems, not written here); one sentence read at a glance, CHF with two decimals and 'about' for estimates ('less than CHF 0.01' under a centime), times in the person's time zone, no ids, no USD, no raw states, no markdown, buttons of at most three words, consequence lines of at most 100 characters; a sentence promises only what the engine does (each 'goes on' line is tested against the engine's outcome in the same test world). Money: 'Use API key' never raises a budget (the dialog's budget field still bounds the session and the figure is capped by it; a budget above what is left this month is refused as today); the widening yes is the person's tap, never skipped; 'Use API key' is offered only when the engine's facts say the other credential serves and the caps have room. Security: no credential value, fingerprint, source id or provider text on any screen; the links go to the setup assistant; card text is data. Do not touch: the engine's rules and the cards' words (d1109-cred-engine), the run indicator's other words and GET /running's shape (d1109-run-visible), the over-budget lines of the Start dialog (d1109-oversize-start), the Basics sections of other areas (d1109-chat-depth's), the sessions list and the session page's header and spend words (d1109-sessions). decisions: 'fix the tasks' (and its synonyms, English and German) is recognised by the parser without a model call; the chat model gets one fix_tasks tool for the same request in other words. Why: no fast-model call before a planning-model call; one path.

The check, the fence and the autonomy rule are d1109-selftasks-run's: from Standard the changes are made by the agent (the planFix context: no read-back, no Inbox echo) and listed with an Undo each, unless a lookup in that turn returned records (d1109-chat-guard's recordsRead: then they are read back at every level); at Advisor and Assisted, or when the set asks first, one composed read-back with Yes and No. Why: the owner's 'autonomy level deciding when it asks first', the same in chat as in a run.

Changes the person names in their own words stay the person's instruction and are read back; several in one line become one question. Why: design §3.9's read-back holds for interpreted instructions; one question per line, never a second card left in the Inbox.
The session page gets an Undo on each change line, from the change log row the event names. Why: 'each change shown with one Undo' where the person sees it.
Changes shows 'In a session' and the agent's name for an agent's change; the task drawer shows what the agent did. Why: design §5 rule 3 (names) and 'every change shown'.
The suggestion card shows its changes open. Why: the person approves what they can read.

fix_tasks takes no request text from the model: its only parameter is the project; the code passes the person's message of that turn verbatim (at most 500 characters) as the request. Why: the design says the person's words are the request; a model-written request could carry text the person never said.

Why: every change shown, plainly, by who made it (design §5 rule 3).

SC-13 (was ST-15): the critic's session review counts a task the agent split, or dropped as a duplicate, as replaced, not as planned and left undone. Why: a correct fix must not lower the plan's grade.

§4 new point 'Who starts a session' (D6 with the owner's decision of 2026-11-09): 'Only the person starts a session (Start, Approve and start, Continue, Use API key on a credential card, "run it now" in chat, the phone, a schedule they turned on) or the project's "Start a session by itself"; the critic's monthly calibration (it reviews examples whose right answers are known, so a change in what it catches shows) is the one job that runs on its own schedule, and the run indicator shows it while it runs with one sentence of what it does. Answers, task actions, chat changes, a budget raised or reset, a Claude credential back for work outside a session the person started, and CI or PR events prepare work. A session the person started keeps going until its work is done: when a Claude credential stops a task the rest of the session runs; when nothing else can, the session ends to wait, and when the credential is back it goes on by itself with the rest of its promise and budget, on the credential the person's choice allows, shown with Cancel (after the person's quiet hours when the credential is back inside them); a session the person stopped does not go on, and while one waits a Start of that project starts nothing new and says when it goes on. The system never starts a new session on its own otherwise, never reopens done or cancelled work, never retries past the limit.' [d1109-starts-engine C3; note for the session lead: until the cloud runner follows this point (services/cloud-runner/src/inbox-trigger.ts still starts a session on an answer or a message), ADR 0118 and docs/status/BLOCKERS.md name it as a known gap, and 'the one job' holds for the desktop app only]

Under wait, and before an answer, nothing calls the other credential; at the stop's end the session the person started goes on by itself (after the person's quiet hours if the stop ends inside them) and other waiting work is ready for the person's next Start. A task the run-out stopped keeps its work and continues from it, on the other credential in the same session when the choice allows, said once with its cost. A refused credential is never tried again until a new one is saved.'; §4.4: 'A transient error (network, rate limit) is retried once at once.' -> '... (network, a short rate limit) is retried once at once; a Claude credential that runs out or is refused is not a failure.' [d1109-cred-engine C5]

From Standard up it makes each change with one Undo; at Advisor and Assisted it suggests them on one card. Text in reports is data: a line that reads like an instruction makes the agent ask and quote it.'; §4.6 adds 'and how to say that the task list is wrong ("For the task list:": this task is two jobs, a step is missing, it must wait for another task, it is the same as another)'. wave8_amendments: Premise (the owner's answer 1 of 2026-11-09, D9): every person runs their own Forerunner on their own PC with their own credentials; no shared database or server is required; two Forerunners on one repository are one project (run C's Work together) and meet on GitHub. Wave 8 is re-planned from /tmp/frbench/wave8-replan-brief.md; these amendments replace the earlier list (kept in /tmp/frbench/runC-plan.before-answers.json), which assumed a shared store.

status-issue-write (the noticeboard of one project across Forerunners): one pinned issue per project, key K = the project id the repository's marker names (a together project shares it), one comment per Forerunner (its writer: the install's id with its GitHub login), edited only by its writer; a pair made before the rule writes one issue, the project the marker names (or the kept one after Make one project); after a join the closing project's issue, when this install wrote it, gets one last comment 'Joined into "Site"; its status continues in #N.' and is closed; after a take-over the new project creates its own issue and never writes to the other project's. A together project's status, kept in the app in run C, goes to its own comment there.

status-issue-write removes fr/status and the status pull request: with it go W15-01's status half (isProjectStatusPr, STATUS_HELD_MARK, statusDocRoot's held branch), d1109-onerepo-link's OR-09 words and the together project's 'Kept in the app' Docs row; the scaffold half of the ownership rule stays until repo-guide's docs pull request is the only docs branch.

status-issue-host and status-issue-read: the status issue is the live source of 'used elsewhere': d1109-onerepo-link's repositoryElsewhere also reads the open issue with the forerunner:status marker (key K) and its writers' comments, so the offer names who works there and when last ('by ada-gh, last active 2 Nov'); issue text stays data (wrapUntrusted, the injection scan); the writers' last activity joins the pull requests' updatedAt (open, merged or closed, as run C reads them) in the 14-day rule; Work together stays the first button.

status-issue-read (claims across Forerunners): before planning and before every task a Forerunner reads the other Forerunners' comments: their 'Working on now' and announced work are left out of its plans and runs (announcements, not locks: the owner's design of 2026-11-02), the plan-only intake's 'Already in the project' block gains 'Announced on GitHub by <login>'s Forerunner' lines (data), and the same files warn first (announced work matches by its files, and its title as data, never by branch: each Forerunner names its task branches by its own task ids, pr-executor.ts taskBranchName); another person's paused task is announced work: this agent does not plan or run it; its handoff is read from the work-in-progress commit message on the pushed branch (pr-executor.ts workInProgressMessage), quoted as data.

status-issue-write: a task paused at a budget is listed as paused with what is done and left (the handoff, quoted as data, no ids) and whether the project's checks pass on its kept work; a pause without progress is listed as waiting for its owner's answer, never as in progress; a session that waits for its Claude credential and goes on by itself is listed as 'waits until 15:40, then it goes on' (information on the other PC, no Cancel).

repo-guide: AGENTS.md's Forerunner part is rendered only by the Forerunner that made the project (the marker's writer); a together project never rewrites it; it says 'This repository is the Forerunner project "<name>". To work on it with Forerunner, link this repository in your own Forerunner and choose Work together; do not start a second project on it. Each Forerunner announces its work in the pinned status issue.' and how any person or agent leaves unfinished work (finish the step, leave the build and the tests passing or name the one that fails, a 'Work in progress: <title>' commit on the task's branch with Where I stopped and Left to do, the next step first; one source for these rules beside wrapUpText).

repo-guide: AGENTS.md and the one-line CLAUDE.md join the doc set that the per-turn excerpts and recall's documents kind read (packages/memory/src/docs-search.ts collectDocFiles :91-130 reads README.md and docs/ only), so 'how do we work in this repository?' finds the guide; STATUS_DOC_RE stays in agent.ts.

status-issue-read: the status issue's comments that Forerunner reads become a recall kind 'status' (quoted as issue_comment data, author and date named; never a block of the default context), marked untrusted so d1109-chat-guard's read-back after records applies; a status case joins the record channel of pnpm test:injection (evals/injection/cases/record-*).

collab-feed (from GitHub, not a store): the other Forerunner's work reaches the person from GitHub: its open and merged pull requests on the project (project mark, task marks this Forerunner does not own), listed as information ('Ada's Forerunner: "Contact form" waits for Merge') with no Merge, no Stop and no link to a page this PC cannot open; its session results and paused work from its status comment; at most one Updates line per session of the other Forerunner, never one per change; each Forerunner merges its own pull requests.

collab-claims (one person's own devices): a paused task's work in progress lives on the computer that ran it unless 'Push unfinished work to GitHub' is on; the other Forerunner never takes such a task (it is announced); a person's own cloud runner and phone on their state service keep today's claims.

collab-journey and collab-bench: two homes, each with its own SQLite store and stand-in credentials, one stand-in GitHub with two users (and an organisation): Ada makes the project; Bob links the repository and chooses Work together; both plan and run; Bob's plan leaves out Ada's announced work; each merges only their own pull requests; a task larger than one session paused in Ada's home is not run by Bob's (announced), and with 'Push unfinished work to GitHub' on Bob sees the branch and its checks; no credential, budget or chat crosses; 'what did Ada's Forerunner do yesterday?' in Bob's chat is answered from the status issue and the pull requests, with names and dates.

D5 to D7 per person, trivially with no shared store: the credential policy, its grants and the ask card are each person's own; the agent's task check changes only its own Forerunner's tasks and never the other Forerunner's announced work; a Continue spends only its presser's budget.

Left to wave 8 deliberately: everything that shows the other Forerunner's work beyond its pull requests on GitHub (the status issue, announced work, the feed from GitHub), the guide's line, removing the status pull request, and any words or actions about the other person beyond 'Shared on GitHub with another Forerunner'; run C promises none of them.

Gone with the shared store (wave 8 builds none of them unless its planner keeps a shared-store mode, an open question of the brief): Ask to join, project.share and its refusal, sharing by name, another person's sessions, chat and spending on a shared store and their privacy rules, the offline outbox for a shared store, the shared-store rules for the hands-off setting and Continue, and the per-person reading of chat's thinking-longer setting (chat_ask_above is simply each person's own).

rules: Live check 4 runs after sub-run C6 is merged and pushed, CI and the Desktop app workflow are green on that head, and in a session started after the owner's 2026-11-09 token update (FORERUNNER_TEST_GITHUB_TOKEN). Live check 3 (wave 15, cap USD 3) runs on run B's merged head before C1, as planned: its G2 builds two projects on one repository, which D1 forbids from C2 on.

Cap USD 6.00 (estimate USD 6.45 for every step; USD 4.37 at priority 1, USD 2.08 at priority 2): priority 1 first in the listed order, then priority 2 in the listed order while the ledger is under USD 5.40 (no new step after USD 5.40), priority 3 last; a step not reached goes to the owner's checklist or the next leftovers; no step is repeated at this cap.

Steps with after_sub_run C2, C4 or C5 cost no model money and may run as soon as that sub-run is merged (early warning before the next sub-run builds on it): LC-C1 after C2 (Work together and the take-over on forerunner-sandbox in two bench homes; the sandbox's leftover bench pull requests #1, #2, #3, #6 and #7 were closed with the owner's yes on 2026-11-09 20:10 UTC), LC-C4 after C4 (Make one project on GitHub), LC-C20 after C5 (the Desktop app workflow's window job on the pushed C5 head, read again after C6) and LC-C31 after C5 (the continuation, no spend; the preset set through settings.set credential_policy, its Settings screen after C6). A failure found early becomes a fix note for the next sub-run's fixers (args.fixNotes) instead of waiting for C6.

Every step uses FORERUNNER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the bench start (--provider bench-live) or in the live harness, never printed, logged or committed; GitHub steps write only to forerunner-sandbox and the person closes what they open.

steps.step: LC-C31 (the owner's decision of 2026-11-09, (a); no model spend): the bench with the subscription stand-in and this environment's real API key saved second (never printed), preset 'Subscription first, then wait' (set through settings.set credential_policy after C5; its Settings screen comes in C6); a person's two-task session whose second task meets the stand-in's limit. Expect: the first task done, the session ending to wait, GET /running and the bar '<project> · waiting until <time>, then it goes on' with Cancel; zero requests to api.anthropic.com during the wait (the harness's request log); at the stand-in's reset exactly one session by 'continuation' with the budget left (the ledger) on the stand-in, its log 'Goes on with your session of <time>.'; quit and start the daemon once during the wait: still one continuation; a second run with Cancel pressed: nothing starts at the reset and the rows read 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.'; a third run with quiet hours set to cover the stand-in's reset: the bar names the end of the quiet hours and the session goes on once then; a fourth with Stop after this task pressed before the stop: the session ends without a continuation and nothing starts at the reset; while one waits, Start on that project answers 'Your session of <time> goes on by itself at <time>.' and starts nothing. A fifth run on a home where nothing was ever chosen: chat, a review and the task's planning make their calls on the subscription stand-in and none on the key (the default preset for every call, the owner's answer 4).
steps.source: runC-plan (owner-decisions-2026-11-09.md, session lead's notes (a)); d1109-starts-engine S-10, d1109-run-visible V-1/V-5, d1109-cred-engine CE-5; the run C check's points on quiet hours, a stopped session and one wait per project
steps.needs: the bench with the subscription stand-in and the real key as the second credential (bench-live harness request log); C5 merged (the indicator and the policy; the policy screens after C6)

owner_checklist_additions: Checklist step 1-2 (fresh install, D1 with D9): New project on forerunner-sandbox shows 'already the Forerunner project "Kite club", which is not on this computer' with its last activity on GitHub ('from your account' when the old install's pull requests were yours), Work together first, then Take it over with the line 'The repository then names this project: choose it only if no Forerunner uses "Kite club" now.'; nobody else uses that bench project, so press Take it over: the docs pull request replaces the marker. (If another GitHub account worked on it within 14 days, in an open, merged or closed pull request, the offer is Work together and Cancel only: that is the multi-person rule working.)

Windows, D1 folder identity (validation rule 5): link a folder, then New project on a subfolder of it (the offer), on a folder with its own git repository inside a broad linked folder (a new project), on a folder on another drive (a new project) and on a path with spaces and accented letters.

Subscription (D2): one task, Stop now mid-run so Claude Code reports late usage; its Sessions row reads 'CHF ... of your Claude subscription's allowance' and, after the late booking, equals the session page and the Overview, with no stored text changed.

Subscription (D4): the research task of LC-C7 with a session budget of CHF 0.40: Claude Code receives the new wrap-up words once as PostToolUse additionalContext (the hook log), and the pause and the card match LC-C7.

Subscription (D3, optional): on a subscription-only install ask 'why does <a failed task> keep failing?': a short answer and the one-line question before a stronger model ('This needs a stronger model: about … seconds on your Claude plan (about CHF … at API prices). Go ahead?'); Go ahead: booked with its plan share, the footer says 'on your Claude plan', the plan-share cap respected; 'think it through' alone thinks longer on the same model without asking; with 'Subscription first, then API key' chosen and the subscription resting, the longer pass asks first and its line names 'on your API key'; under the default 'then wait' chat instead says it has not answered and offers 'Use API key'.
If two projects on one repository exist from before (D1): the Overview line, Make one project, a moved pull request merged from the kept project, and Undo after quitting and reopening Forerunner.

Start a session on a project; while it runs go to Home, Inbox, Settings, another project and open Talk: each shows one bar with the project, what it does now and Stop; hover the Forerunner window in the taskbar and the tray icon: both name the project; close the window to the tray: the tray menu's first line says what runs and the icon has a dot (also on Linux, where only a unit test checks the dot, and the window title there); when the session ends, nothing shows anywhere; if the critic's monthly check runs while you look (day 1 at 06:00), the bar shows 'Forerunner · the critic's monthly check on known examples' with Stop, and opening it says what it does.

With nothing running, answer an Inbox question: no session starts; the Done line says 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.' with a Start button; the project's line says 'Ready: 1 task waits for your Start'.
Add two tasks in chat, change one of them, write a note, then say 'run it now' and press Yes: only then does a session start; saying 'ok' or 'sounds good' starts nothing.

While a session runs, Redo a small done task: it says 'It joins the session that is running.' and runs before the session ends; Make ready a large one: it says it waits for your next Start and does not run.
In Settings, turn on 'When work is ready: Start a session by itself' for one project and answer a card there: a session starts; turn it off again.

If your Claude subscription reaches its limit during a session you started with 'Subscription first, then wait': the other tasks still run, then the session ends to wait and the bar under the header on every page (and Talk, the tray tooltip) says '<project> · waiting until <time>, then it goes on' with Cancel; at that time the session goes on by itself on your subscription with the rest of its budget (nothing runs on the API key, and it is not a new full-budget session). In another wait press Stop after this task before it ends to wait: nothing goes on by itself at the reset. If your quiet hours cover the reset, the bar says when they end and the session goes on then. While it waits, Start on that project says when your session goes on and starts nothing new. In another wait press Cancel: nothing starts at the reset, the project says 'Ready: N tasks wait for your Start' and the session's Continue offers the rest with its budget left. With no session of yours waiting, press Start while the subscription is at its limit and choose 'Start at <time>': the project says 'Starts at <time>' with Cancel, and it starts then.
Raise the monthly cap while a task is paused at it: nothing starts; the Settings line says it is ready for your Start.
In the tray menu, 'Stop all sessions' stops the running session and nothing starts until you choose 'Allow sessions again'.

Install the run C build (Desktop app workflow), keep the project at Standard, and give it a brief whose plan has a task that is clearly two jobs (for example 'Make a one-page site with a contact form, styled, and publish it'). Start. When a task's report says the task list needs a change, see on the session page one line per change with an Undo, and the new tasks on the Tasks tab with what they wait for.

Press Undo on one of those lines on the session page: see only that change taken back (the task as it was, the new part gone) and the others left; see the same row marked Undone in Changes, labelled 'In a session'.
At the session's end see one Update for it in the Inbox (with 'changed N tasks'), not one per change.

Set the project to Assisted (Settings, autonomy by name) and run another session: see one card 'the agent suggests N changes to the tasks' with the changes listed, the session going on meanwhile; press Make these changes and see one Changes row with one Undo; no new session starts by itself.

In the project's chat, type 'fix the tasks': see 'Checking the tasks…' while it works, then at Assisted one question listing the changes, at Standard the changes each with an Undo; nothing starts a session.

With a subscription-first choice in Settings, Basics, 'Which Claude does the work', run one session where a task check happens: see the check's cost in CHF on the session page and the subscription allowance moving; nothing over the session budget. With no choice made, the check, chat, planning and reviews use your subscription first like the tasks (your answer 4).
Check the money: with a small session budget, see work the agent added named under 'Left for your next Start' instead of run, and no session starting until you press Start.
Read every new line (session page, card, Update, chat, task drawer): one plain sentence each, CHF, no ids, no raw states.

Open Settings: Basics shows 'Which Claude does the work' under Accounts and keys with your earlier choice selected (or, if you never set an order, 'Subscription first, then wait' selected and marked 'Used until you choose'), both credentials in order with their state now, and one line saying what happens if the first runs out. Advanced has no Move up / Move down and no 'When my first choice runs out mid-session' row.
Pick 'Subscription first, ask before API key': it changes at once and Changes lists it with Undo. Pick 'Subscription first, then API key': a yes is asked first, saying it costs money.

With 'ask before API key', when your plan's limit is reached during a session: one Inbox card 'Use your API key until ...?' with the reset time in your time and the cost. Press Wait: your API key's spend in Settings and Costs does not move, no second card comes for that limit, the bar says 'waiting until <time>, then it goes on', and at the reset your session goes on by itself on the subscription. At the next limit press Use API key: the session goes on at once, and the task's drawer, the session page and Costs -> By credential show the work on your API key with its cost. After the reset, the next tasks use your subscription again.

With 'Subscription first, then wait' and your subscription at its limit: nothing runs on the API key while it waits; chat says it has not answered and offers 'Use API key', which spends only when you press it; no reminder arrives while it waits; the session you started goes on by itself when the subscription is back.

With 'Subscription first, then API key' and your subscription at its limit: the work goes on with the API key by itself, one desktop notification says so with the cost, and the session's result names what the API key part cost.

Lower the subscription allowance so Forerunner's share is reached during a task: the task follows your choice (goes on with the API key, asks, or waits until the 1st) and no budget card appears; raising the allowance again ends the wait: the Settings line says your session goes on, the session you started goes on by itself on the subscription, and work outside a session of yours reads Ready for your Start.

Paste a wrong API key in the setup assistant, or let your subscription sign-in expire: one card says what was refused, why in plain words, how to save a new one and what the work does meanwhile, with one notification; your Anthropic console shows one failed request, not repeated attempts.

The Start dialog and an unapproved plan card each say in one line what happens if your first choice runs out; with your subscription at its limit the Start dialog offers 'Use API key' and 'Start at 15:40'.
With a real Claude Code limit (the 5-hour or weekly one), the reset time on the card, the rows and the Start dialog matches what Claude Code reports.
Quit and reopen: the choice, any 'Use API key' answer you gave and any open card are kept until the subscription is back, and a session waiting to go on still goes on once at the reset.

Two Forerunners, one repository (D9, your answer 1): on a second PC signed in to GitHub with another account (the desktop app runs once per computer: two installs on one PC are a testing setup through FORERUNNER_HOME, not this check), link the repository of a project your first Forerunner uses: the offer is Work together and Cancel (with your own account on both PCs, Take it over is offered second, with its warning line); press Work together: nothing changes on GitHub at the press; the Overview says 'Shared on GitHub with another Forerunner: each keeps its own tasks.'; run one task in each: each Forerunner lists and merges only its own pull request.

A task larger than its session (D4, your answer 5): give a large task the highest priority with a small one behind it: the Start dialog says the large one works until the budget is used and the small one comes after it and runs only if budget is left; Start: the large one starts first, wraps up and pauses with one card; with the small one first in priority, the small one runs first; later press Start without answering the card: the large one goes on in its turn from where it stopped and its card closes.

Chat (D3, your answer 2): 'think it through: what did the last two sessions do?' thinks longer on the same model without asking; 'use a stronger model: why does <a failed task> keep failing?' asks once with the cost and the time, and only Go ahead (or 'yes') starts it; with 'Chat asks first' in Settings, Basics at 0, 'think it through' asks too.

One order (D5, your answer 4): on a fresh install with both credentials saved and nothing chosen, Settings, Basics shows 'Subscription first, then wait' selected and marked 'Used until you choose'; a chat question and a plan run on your subscription (the API key's line in Costs does not move).

Run C's sessions list, chat and Make one project on the installed build (Desktop app workflow of the pushed run C head): U-089 to U-096's Check in the app steps, each once, as the session lead lists them in UPDATE-LOG.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D5, after your answer 4): until you pick in Settings, 'Subscription first, then wait' is used for every call, chat included, so at your subscription's limit chat waits too (it still offers a one-off 'Use API key'). Should the default be 'Subscription first, ask before API key' instead?
owner_questions.default_built: Subscription first, then wait (your default of 2026-11-02), now for every call; a session you started goes on by itself when the subscription is back.
owner_questions.why: 'Ask first' did not exist when you chose 'wait'; it would file a card with a cost at every run-out for people who never chose.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D3, after your answer 2): chat now thinks longer as needed, with no daily amount of its own; its spend counts against the project's budget as well as the monthly cap, as all chat spend does today. Should longer answers count only against the monthly cap, so thinking in chat never takes budget from the project's work?
owner_questions.default_built: Counted against the project's budget and the monthly cap; chat asks first before a stronger model or an answer over CHF 0.10.
owner_questions.why: With no daily amount, chat's thinking can take room a project's sessions need; it is a money rule.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D6, a session that waits for Claude): if you set quiet hours and your Claude credential comes back inside them (the share comes back at 00:00 UTC on the 1st, for example), should a session you started go on at once, or wait until your quiet hours end?
owner_questions.default_built: It waits until they end, because your Quiet hours setting says 'no sessions that start on their own between these times'; the bar says 'waiting until 07:00 (after your quiet hours), then it goes on' and Cancel works as before.
owner_questions.why: Your decision of 2026-11-09 says the session goes on when the credential is back but did not mention quiet hours; waiting moves nothing and keeps the setting's promise, going on at once keeps the work moving at night. One rule in the scheduler changes.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D5): under 'Subscription first, then wait', the Start dialog and chat still offer a one-off 'Use API key' that spends only when you press it. Keep that, or offer it only under 'ask before API key'?
owner_questions.why: 'Wait' means the app does nothing by itself, not that you cannot choose; but it puts a money button in front of someone who chose to wait.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D1): two projects that already share a repository (made before this change) keep working until you make them one, or should the newer one's sessions be held?
owner_questions.default_built: Both keep working; each Overview asks with Make one project; W15-01 keeps their pull requests apart.
owner_questions.why: Keep today's behaviour where the owner did not decide; holding work is a new stop.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D5): should the API key get its own monthly limit in Forerunner ('at most CHF 20 a month on the API key')?
owner_questions.default_built: No: Anthropic's own spend limit and your monthly cap bound it; a limit stored by an earlier version still counts as running out.
owner_questions.why: Not asked for yet; it would be a new limit level in the hooks.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D6): should 'When work is ready: Start a session by itself' also have an app-wide default for new projects in Settings, Basics?
owner_questions.default_built: Per project only, off for every project.
owner_questions.why: One project can run hands-off while you are still shaping another.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D7): a task that failed after its tries: should its card also offer 'Split it'?
owner_questions.default_built: The card stays as today (Try again, Mark done anyway, Cancel task); 'split X' in chat does it, read back.
owner_questions.why: One more option on a card that already has three.

owner_questions.question: Owner (D7): should 'Fix the tasks' also be a button on the Tasks tab?
owner_questions.default_built: Chat only, plus the agent's own check during a run.
owner_questions.why: One more button on the Tasks tab.

session_lead_decisions: Not open, and built: (a) a session the person started goes on by itself when its Claude credential is back, as the person's own start continuing, shown on the run indicator with Cancel, never on another credential unless the policy says so, while a NEW session after a stop the person did not start needs the person or the hands-off setting; (b) the agent changes its own tasks without asking from Standard up and asks first at Advisor and Assisted. Both are the owner's (session lead's notes of 2026-11-09 16:35 UTC) and are removed from the open questions.

Areas: the 14 areas of the two specs are kept, no merge and no split: each is 7 to 15 items, the D1-D4 revision already split oversize (start/pause) and chat (guard/recall/depth) along their boundaries, and merging any two would pass the size one fixer finishes well. d1109-selftasks-chat's SC-14 (added by the first plan) is kept but narrowed to chat's 'fix the tasks' when the check is held; the run's task check under the policy is d1109-cred-engine's again (CE-3, CE-7), now that it merges after d1109-selftasks-run.

Order: six sub-runs (C1 d1109-chat-guard, d1109-oversize-start, d1109-sessions; C2 d1109-onerepo-link, d1109-chat-recall, d1109-oversize-pause; C3 d1109-starts-engine, d1109-chat-depth; C4 d1109-onerepo-join, d1109-selftasks-run; C5 d1109-cred-engine, d1109-run-visible; C6 d1109-cred-screens, d1109-selftasks-chat). The first plan's five were one too few: d1109-cred-engine needs d1109-selftasks-run's task check (CE-3's table row, CE-7's ask card, the prompt assertions; task-check.ts does not exist at 3600089) and d1109-onerepo-join must see d1109-starts-engine's continuation, so the longest chain is d1109-oversize-start -> d1109-oversize-pause -> d1109-starts-engine -> d1109-selftasks-run -> d1109-cred-engine -> d1109-cred-screens. With concurrency 2 a three-area sub-run already takes two rounds, so six sub-runs of 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2 cost about the same wall time as five of 3, 3, 3, 3, 2, plus one merge step, and fewer files are shared inside a sub-run (runner.ts, executor.ts and request-words.ts no longer meet in one). Security and data integrity first (d1109-chat-guard in C1, d1109-onerepo-link in C2 before d1109-onerepo-join in C4, which comes first in C4's key order), the engine before its screens (d1109-starts-engine C3 before d1109-run-visible C5; d1109-cred-engine C5 before d1109-cred-screens C6).

d1109-sessions stays in C1 (the D5-D8 spec wanted it after d1109-starts-engine and d1109-run-visible): its startedByWords reads plan.startedBy ({by, continues}, the shape fixed in this plan) before the trigger, d1109-starts-engine adds the 'hands_off' and 'continuation' words in that function, and d1109-run-visible re-points workingWords at runText; until C5 the working row uses the project status's working sentence. d1109-chat-recall and d1109-onerepo-join get sessionGist and projectSessionsView without fallbacks.

ADR numbers in merge order, one sequence: 0114 chat (d1109-chat-guard), 0115 a task larger than one session (d1109-oversize-start), 0116 sessions list (d1109-sessions), 0117 one repository one project (d1109-onerepo-link), 0118 who starts a session with D8 (d1109-starts-engine), 0119 the agent keeps its task list right (d1109-selftasks-run), 0120 which Claude does the work (d1109-cred-engine). The D1-D4 spec's 0114 (d1109-sessions) and 0116 (d1109-chat-guard's chat ADR) swap; 0115 and 0117 to 0120 are as that spec proposed; the D5-D8 spec's numbers are replaced.

U-entries in merge order of the owning area: U-089 larger task, U-090 sessions list, U-091 one repository, U-092 chat recall (with d1109-chat-guard's step), U-093 who starts a session, U-094 chat thinks longer, U-095 the agent's task list, U-096 a running session everywhere; d1109-cred-engine and d1109-cred-screens amend U-078, U-052, U-048 and U-074 instead of a new entry (U-078 is the owner's 'Wait' entry).

The continuation, built in d1109-starts-engine S-10 (details the owner left to the build, revised by the run C check): StartRequest.by gains 'continuation'; it is kept for sessions by 'person' or 'continuation', and for a session a schedule the person set started (today the handover test; the owner's D6 list counts 'a schedule they set' as the person saying when), never for the critic's calibration (its held call skips and stays due) and never for a session the person stopped (Stop after this task, Stop now) or that was stopping or wrapping up when it ended to wait; it carries the cap less the ledger's booked spend and the remaining promise (never a fresh full budget; none when nothing is left); it starts once at whatever ends the stop (the reset, a raised allowance, the month's start for the share, a new key saved after a refusal), on the credential the policy allows; quiet hours hold it like every start the person did not press (the Quiet hours setting promises 'no sessions that start on their own'; built so, and asked); Stop all, Cancel and the project's removal (w15-tail's guard) drop it; Make one project is refused while it waits. One wait per project: while a continuation or a kept start waits, a person start of that project keeps and starts nothing and says when it goes on (the first plan let a newer Start replace it, which contradicted its own Start dialog); a person start kept for the reset ('Start at 15:40') is offered only when no session of the project waits to go on.

The run indicator shows a person's session waiting to go on ('Quote page · waiting until 15:40, then it goes on', the owner's words, with Cancel; 'waiting until 07:00 (after your quiet hours)' when those end later; a generic 'waiting for Claude' for the share and key-month stops until d1109-cred-screens words them in C6); a held hands-off start and a person start kept for the reset are said on the project's status line only; while only a session waits, the tray tooltip and menu say it but the window title, the browser title and the tray dot stay as when nothing runs (they mean a session runs now). The critic's monthly check ('the critic's monthly check on known examples', with one sentence of what it does: the owner's answer 6) is shown while it runs, with Stop: D8 ('very clear when a run is ongoing, no matter where the person is') decides that, so it is not an owner question.

D4's 'goes on by itself' at an outer limit: a limit raised or reset only prepares (d1109-starts-engine S-3); the person's own session waiting for its Claude credential goes on as in (a), and the subscription's share joins that case when d1109-cred-engine makes it a credential stop (C5); until then a share pause is a budget card that prepares.

Settings keys in merge order: start_by_itself, chat_ask_above (was chat_thinks_longer, a daily amount, until the owner's answer 2 of 2026-11-09; now the amount above which one chat answer asks first), credential_policy; both C3 areas append from one base and the merge step keeps both lines.

Whole-list tests (the chat's tool list, the settings_set definition) are re-baselined by the merge step of C2 and C3, where two areas change them from one base; each area asserts its own definitions' exact text.

repo.take_over's 'Took over' row on Changes is the command's own change sentence (GET /changes renders every command's sentence), so d1109-onerepo-link never edits d1109-chat-recall's extracted row-words function in their shared sub-run.

recordsRead, CommandOutcome.untrusted and the injection 'record' channel are d1109-chat-guard's (the D5-D8 spec named d1109-chat-recall); d1109-selftasks-run's 'report' channel follows 'record'; its cases are report-001 to report-006.
Migration 0009 is d1109-selftasks-run's: no other run C area adds a migration (plan JSON, summary_cache, settings keys and BillingSourceLimits fields need none).

Kept from the D1-D4 spec's 'session lead' questions as built defaults, not owner questions: a project removed by Undo of its creation frees its repository (took_over with removed true, the marker replaced by the next project's first docs pull request); the run again in the session at the specialist's limit per run is for the larger task only; the hold that moved a larger task behind the tasks that fit (also in the first session after a plan's approval) is removed in C2 by d1109-oversize-pause's OP-0 (the owner's answer 5: the larger task runs in its turn, the tasks after it take what it leaves, and the next start continues a task paused at a session's budget and closes its card, decided from answer 5's 'continue next time' and not asked again); the kept-work check runs at every pause whose kept work changed a code file; voice and the phone get no thinking longer in run C.

Run B's guards stay through run C: w15-tail's removed-project refusal in startSession and POST /sessions and its skip in credentialWaits.wake (d1109-starts-engine keeps them; a continuation of a removed project is dropped), W15B-01's folder hold in pr-executor.ts (no run C area changes pr-executor.ts; an immediate answer at the Redo itself stays out of scope).

Live checks: live check 3 (cap USD 3) runs on run B's head before C1 as planned; run C's real-model steps of both specs (USD 2.98 and USD 3.47) and one zero-cost continuation step are one live check 4 after C6 with its own cap of USD 6.00 (live check 2's cap was USD 7.25, spent USD 4.03), priority 1 first and no new step after USD 5.40; zero-cost steps may run early: LC-C1 after C2, LC-C4 after C4, LC-C20 and LC-C31 after C5.

Design document and registry: the session lead edits docs/design/core-experience.md from design_doc_changes after the sub-run that builds each change, and syncs conversation-agent 1.3.0 (after C2) and 1.4.0 (after C3) to forerunner-registry.

The plan does not touch the repository; the session lead appends the 14 areas (with sub_run, wave and plan_corrections) and the run C shared_files rules to /tmp/frbench/phaseE.json, then runs forerunner-phase-e6.js once per sub-run with args {wave, keys, note} from sub_runs.

CHANGELOG.md is taken out of every area's files[] and out of shared_files rule 'Docs': the pipeline's common prompt tells every fixer not to edit CHANGELOG.md, docs/status/UPDATE-LOG.md or docs/requirements.md (the session lead writes them from the reports), and run B's areas do not list it either.
d1109-cred-screens' items are renamed CS-1 to CS-10 so that 'V-n' always means d1109-run-visible's item; every reference in the plan follows.

The share's and a key's monthly cap's waits end at the month's start UTC; every sentence names that moment in the person's time zone ('Tue 1 Dec, 01:00'), or the end of the quiet hours when later. The words for such a waiting session on the indicator, the status line and the session page are d1109-cred-screens' (C6, built after both d1109-cred-engine and d1109-run-visible); until then d1109-run-visible shows the generic form.

The Settings change line for a raised subscription allowance is d1109-cred-engine's (CE-6) once the share is a credential stop: it says the person's waiting session goes on (or when, inside quiet hours), else that the tasks are ready for the next Start; d1109-starts-engine's S-3 line covers the monthly cap and the project budget. The share's Wait line on the ask card has the same two forms as the limit's.

The critic's calibration stays on by default and monthly (requirement H.7, ADR 0060), confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-09 (answer 6); it is shown on the run indicator (D8) with words saying what it does. What it is for, as told to the owner: once a month the critic (the reviewer that checks every finished task) reviews a fixed set of examples whose right answers are known (good work and work with planted mistakes); the share it catches and the share it passes are compared with the month before, so a drift in its judgement (after a model or prompt change) shows before it lets bad work through or sends good work back; it spends at most USD 10 (about CHF 8 to 9) a month from its own budget (on the Claude plan, under the default preset, counted at API prices) and sends one notification with the result.

The cloud runner (services/cloud-runner/src/inbox-trigger.ts) still asks for a session with trigger 'message' on a new message or an answered request; it stays out of scope this round, and ADR 0118, the design note for 'Who starts a session' and docs/status/BLOCKERS.md (the session lead's) name it as a known gap, so 'the one exception' is said for this computer only. It is not an owner question: D6 already says what it should do.

The D5-D8 spec's owner_explanation (15 points) is superseded by this plan's owner_summary; its points 7 ('When it is back nothing starts by itself') and 13 ('Wait means nothing moves') contradict the owner's decision (a) and must not be sent to the owner again.

owner_summary: Run C builds your eight decisions of 9 November (D1 to D8) and your ten answers of that evening as 14 pieces of work in six steps, one after the other.
Step 1 (being built now): chat treats what it reads as information, never as orders; a task too big for one session runs anyway; every project lists its sessions.

Step 2: one repository belongs to one project, and a second person's Forerunner on it works on that same project ('Work together': joining changes nothing on GitHub, neither Forerunner touches the other's pull requests, and each opens its own for its own tasks); chat can look up anything recorded; a big task runs in its turn like any task, pauses cleanly, and goes on from where it stopped at your next Start (or at once with its card's Continue).

Your question 'Isn't this already built in cleanly?': no. Today two Forerunners on one repository share only git: each keeps its own tasks and cards, so both could plan the same work. Step 2 makes them one project; wave 8 then lets each see the other's work on GitHub (a pinned status issue, announced work, a guide in the repository). No shared database is needed: each person keeps their own API key and subscription on their own PC.

Step 3: only you start sessions (answers and changes prepare work); a session you started goes on by itself after a Claude wait; chat thinks longer when it helps and asks you first, with the cost and the time, before a stronger model or an answer over CHF 0.10 (on your Claude plan: the same amount at API prices, so using up your plan counts too).

Step 4: two projects on one repository can become one, also a project here with another person's (Work together); the agent fixes its own task list during a run (by itself from Standard, asking first at Advisor and Assisted; your own tasks only by suggestion).

Step 5: one order for every call, the one you pick, and what happens when it runs out; until you pick, 'Subscription first, then wait' for everything; a bar on every screen, in the tray and the window title shows what runs, with Stop.
Step 6: that choice in one clean menu in Settings, in the Start dialog and on the cards; 'fix the tasks' in chat.

What the critic's monthly check is for (your answer 6): the critic is the reviewer that checks every finished task before it counts as done. On the 1st of each month it reviews a fixed set of examples whose right answers are known (good work, and work with planted mistakes), and what it catches is compared with the month before. So if a model or prompt update makes it start letting bad work through, or sending good work back, you see it before it costs you. It has its own budget of about CHF 8 a month (on your Claude plan when that is your first choice) and sends one notification with the result; the bar shows it while it runs.

Your answer 3 ('For all work'): a yes on 'Use your API key until …?' covers all your work and chat in every project until your subscription is back. Forerunner's own monthly checks (the model watch and the critic's check) are not your work: they wait for the subscription, which costs nothing, and the card says so.
Each step is about 5 to 7 hours of agent work, so about 30 to 42 hours, then one real-model check capped at USD 6 and your install-and-check list.

Your ten answers are built in. Decided from your own words, not asked again: your next Start continues a large task that paused at its session's budget (its card closes; its Continue still goes on at once); tasks planned after it use what it leaves. Where a question is still open the safe choice is built: a waiting session does not go on inside your quiet hours.
9 questions stay open (21 before your answers); the biggest: whether 'ask first' should replace 'wait' as the default, and whether chat's longer answers should count only against the monthly cap.
Nothing in run C raises a budget or passes a cap; when the app says it waits, nothing moves.

Left for later: the phone (phase H), the cloud runner (it still starts sessions on answers), and seeing each other's work through GitHub (wave 8, re-planned around your answer 1: the status issue, announced work, the repository guide; no shared database).
